sentences.zh: 史昭，合肥人。

translations.literal: Shi Zhao was a man of Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhao was a native of Hefei.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，積功至都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle, through accumulated merit he reached Vice Commander-in-Chief of the Regional Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yongle reign, through accumulated merit he rose to vice commander-in-chief of the regional military commission.

sentences.zh: 八年充總兵官，鎮涼州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he served as supreme commander and garrisoned Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed supreme commander and stationed at Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 土軍老的罕先與千戶虎保作亂，虎保敗，老的罕就撫。

translations.literal: The native soldier Laodiehan had first joined the chiliarch Hubao in rebellion; Hubao was defeated, and Laodiehan submitted to pacification.
translations.idiomatic: The native officer Laodiehan had first joined the chiliarch Hubao in revolt; when Hubao was defeated, Laodiehan accepted pacification.

sentences.zh: 昭上書言其必叛狀。

translations.literal: Zhao memorialized the throne, stating the signs that he would surely rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao memorialized the throne describing how he was certain to rebel.

sentences.zh: 未至，而老的罕果叛。

translations.literal: Before it arrived, Laodiehan did in fact rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Before the memorial arrived, Laodiehan did rebel.

sentences.zh: 昭與都指揮滿都等擊平之。

translations.literal: Zhao together with Regional Commander Mandu and others attacked and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, together with Regional Commander Mandu and others, attacked and suppressed the revolt.

sentences.zh: 移鎮西寧。

translations.literal: He was transferred to garrison Xining.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to garrison Xining.

sentences.zh: 仁宗立，進都督僉事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong ascended the throne, he was promoted to Vice Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 上言西寧風俗鄙悍，請設學校如中土。

translations.literal: He memorialized that Xining's customs were crude and fierce, and requested that schools be established as in the central provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that Xining's customs were crude and fierce and asked that schools be established as in the heartland.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The reply was approval.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，昭以衛軍守禦，不暇屯種，其家屬願力田者七百七十余人，請俾耕藝，收其賦以足軍食。

translations.literal: Early in Xuande, because Zhao's guard troops were occupied with defense and had no time for farming, more than 770 of their dependents who wished to work the fields petitioned to be allowed to cultivate and pay tax in kind to supplement military provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xuande reign, with guard troops tied to defense and no time for farming, more than seven hundred and seventy dependents who wished to till the soil asked permission to farm and pay grain tax to supplement military rations.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The petition was granted.

sentences.zh: 五年，曲先衛都指揮使散即思邀劫西域使臣，昭率參將趙安偕中官王安、王瑾討之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Sanjisi, Regional Commander of the Quxian Guard, waylaid and robbed envoys from the Western Regions; Zhao led Assistant Commander Zhao An together with the eunuchs Wang An and Wang Jin to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Sanjisi, regional commander of the Quxian Guard, waylaid and robbed envoys from the Western Regions; Zhao led Assistant Commander Zhao An and the eunuchs Wang An and Wang Jin against him.

sentences.zh: 長驅至曲先，散即思望風遁，擒其黨答答不花等，獲男女三百四十人，馬駝牛羊三十余萬，威震塞外。

translations.literal: They pressed straight to Quxian; Sanjisi fled at the sight of them; they captured his partisans including Dadabuhua and took 340 men and women, more than 300,000 horses, camels, cattle, and sheep—their prestige shook the lands beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: They drove straight to Quxian; Sanjisi fled at their approach; they seized his followers, including Dadabuhua, and took three hundred and forty men and women and more than three hundred thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep—their fame shook the frontier.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，璽書慰勞，賞賚加等。

translations.literal: When news of the victory arrived, an imperial letter of consolation and commendation was sent, with rewards above the usual scale.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, an imperial letter of praise arrived, with rewards above the usual scale.

sentences.zh: 七年春，以征西將軍鎮寧夏。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year he was made General Who Pacifies the West and garrisoned Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year he was made General Who Pacifies the West and stationed at Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 孛的達裏麻犯邊，遣兵擊之。

translations.literal: When Beddalima raided the border, he dispatched troops to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: When Beddalima raided the border, he sent troops against him.

sentences.zh: 至闊臺察罕，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Reaching Kuotaichahan, they took a great multitude captive.
translations.idiomatic: At Kuotaichahan they captured a great host.

sentences.zh: 進都督同知。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 正統初，昭以寧夏孤懸河外，東抵綏德二千里，曠遠難守，請於花馬池築哨馬營，增設烽堠，直接哈剌兀速之境。

translations.literal: Early in Zhengtong, Zhao noted that Ningxia stood isolated beyond the Yellow River, two thousand li east to Suide, vast and hard to hold; he requested that scout-horse camps be built at Huamachi, beacon towers added, extending straight to the territory of Halawusu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengtong reign, Zhao argued that Ningxia stood alone beyond the river, two thousand li from Suide to the east—too vast to hold—and asked that scout-horse camps be built at Huamachi with new beacon towers reaching to the Halawusu frontier.

sentences.zh: 邊備大固。

translations.literal: Frontier defenses were greatly strengthened.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier defenses were greatly strengthened.

sentences.zh: 尋進右都督。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was promoted to Right Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to right commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時阿臺、朵兒只伯數寇邊。

translations.literal: At the time Atai and Du'erzhibo repeatedly raided the border.
translations.idiomatic: Atai and Du'erzhibo were then raiding the border again and again.

sentences.zh: 詔昭與甘肅守將蔣貴、趙安進剿。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhao together with Gansu's garrison commanders Jiang Gui and Zhao An to advance in punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Zhao, together with Gansu's garrison commanders Jiang Gui and Zhao An, to advance in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 並無功，被昭切責，貶都督僉事。

translations.literal: Neither achieved success; Zhao was sternly rebuked and demoted to Vice Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Neither achieved success; Zhao was sharply rebuked and demoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 三年復右都督，八年以老召還。

translations.literal: In the third year he was restored to Right Commissioner-in-Chief; in the eighth year, on account of age, he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was restored as right commissioner-in-chief; in the eighth year he was recalled on account of age.

sentences.zh: 明年卒。

translations.literal: The following year he died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died.

sentences.zh: 昭居寧夏十二年，老成持重，兵政修舉，亦會敵勢衰弱，邊境得無事。

translations.literal: Zhao resided at Ningxia for twelve years, steady and deliberate in bearing; military administration was well maintained, and it happened also that the enemy's strength waned, so the border knew no disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao held Ningxia for twelve years, steady and deliberate; military affairs were kept in good order, and as enemy strength waned the border remained quiet.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書王驥、寧夏參將王榮嘗舉其過。

translations.literal: Minister of War Wang Ji and Ningxia Assistant Commander Wang Rong once reported his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Wang Ji and Ningxia assistant commander Wang Rong once reported his faults.

sentences.zh: 朝議，以昭守邊久，習兵事，不易也。

translations.literal: At court it was argued that Zhao had long guarded the frontier and was versed in military affairs—he should not be replaced lightly.
translations.idiomatic: At court it was held that Zhao had long guarded the frontier and knew military affairs too well to be replaced lightly.

sentences.zh: 而與昭並為邊將最久、有勛績可稱者，都督同知劉昭鎮西寧二十年；

translations.literal: Those who, like Zhao, had served longest as frontier generals with merit worth noting included Assistant Commissioner Liu Zhao, who garrisoned Xining for twenty years;
translations.idiomatic: Among frontier generals who, like Zhao, had served longest with merit worth noting were Assistant Commissioner Liu Zhao, who garrisoned Xining for twenty years,

sentences.zh: 都指揮李達鎮洮州至四十年。

translations.literal: and Regional Commander Li Da, who garrisoned Taozhou for as long as forty years.
translations.idiomatic: and Regional Commander Li Da, who held Taozhou for as long as forty years.

sentences.zh: 並為蕃漢所畏服。

translations.literal: Both were feared and respected by Tibetans and Chinese alike.
translations.idiomatic: Both were feared and obeyed by Tibetans and Chinese alike.

sentences.zh: 劉昭，全椒人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhao was a man of Quanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao was a native of Quanjiao.

sentences.zh: 永樂五年以都指揮同知使朵甘、烏思藏，建驛站。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongle, as Assistant Regional Commander he was sent to Do-kham and Ü-Tsang to establish postal stations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yongle, as assistant regional commander he was sent to Do-kham and Ü-Tsang to establish relay stations.

sentences.zh: 還至靈藏，番賊邀劫，昭敗之。

translations.literal: On the return at Lingzang, bandits of the border peoples waylaid them; Zhao defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On the return at Lingzang, frontier bandits waylaid them; Zhao defeated them.

sentences.zh: 進都指揮使，鎮河州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Regional Commander and garrisoned Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to regional commander and stationed at Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年，副陳懷討平松潘寇。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuande, as second-in-command to Chen Huai he campaigned to pacify the Songpan marauders.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuande he served under Chen Huai in pacifying the Songpan raiders.

sentences.zh: 累進都督同知，移西寧。

translations.literal: He rose in stages to Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief and was transferred to Xining.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to assistant commissioner-in-chief and was transferred to Xining.

sentences.zh: 復鎮河州，兼轄西寧。

translations.literal: He returned to garrison Hezhou, with concurrent jurisdiction over Xining.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Hezhou, with concurrent authority over Xining.

sentences.zh: 罕東酋劄兒加邀殺中官使西域者，奪璽書金幣去。

translations.literal: The chief of Handom, Zhā'erjia, waylaid and killed the eunuch envoy to the Western Regions and seized the imperial patent, gold, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhā'erjia, chief of Handom, waylaid and killed the eunuch envoy to the Western Regions and seized the imperial patent, gold, and silks.

sentences.zh: 命昭副甘肅總兵官劉廣討之。

translations.literal: An order was issued for Zhao to serve under Gansu's supreme commander Liu Guang to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was ordered to serve under Gansu's supreme commander Liu Guang against him.

sentences.zh: 劄兒加請還所掠書幣，貢馬贖罪。

translations.literal: Zhā'erjia requested to return what he had looted and offered horses in tribute to atone for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Zhā'erjia asked to return what he had seized and offered horses in tribute to atone.

sentences.zh: 帝以窮寇不足深治，命昭等還。

translations.literal: The emperor held that a cornered foe need not be pursued to the utmost, and ordered Zhao and the others to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that a cornered foe need not be pressed further and ordered Zhao and the others to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 李達，定遠人。

translations.literal: Li Da was a man of Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Da was a native of Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 累官都督僉事。

translations.literal: Through successive offices he rose to Vice Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive offices he rose to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 正統中，致仕。

translations.literal: During the Zhengtong reign he retired.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 巫凱，句容人。

translations.literal: Wu Kai was a man of Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kai was a native of Jurong.

sentences.zh: 由廬州衛百戶積功至都指揮同知。

translations.literal: From a centurion of the Luzhou Guard he rose through merit to Assistant Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: From a centurion in the Luzhou Guard he rose through merit to assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 永樂六年以從英國公張輔平交阯功，遷遼東都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongle, for following the Duke of Ying, Zhang Fu, in pacifying Jiaozhi, he was transferred to Regional Commander of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yongle, for following the Duke of Ying, Zhang Fu, in pacifying Jiaozhi, he was made regional commander of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 十一年召帥所部會北京。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was summoned to lead his command to assemble at Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was summoned to lead his troops to assemble at Beijing.

sentences.zh: 明年從征沙漠，命先還。

translations.literal: The next year he accompanied the expedition into the desert and was ordered to return ahead.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he joined the desert campaign and was ordered to return ahead.

sentences.zh: 凱言諸衛兵宜以三之二守禦，而以其一屯糧，開原市馬悉給本衛乘操。

translations.literal: Kai said that of the guards' troops two-thirds should man the defenses and one-third farm; horses purchased at the Kaiyuan market should all be allotted to his guard for riding and drill.
translations.idiomatic: Kai proposed that guard troops should keep two-thirds on defense and one-third on farming, and that horses bought at the Kaiyuan market should all go to his guard for riding and drill.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 宣宗立，以都督僉事佩征虜前將軍印，代朱榮鎮遼東。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, Kai was made Vice Commissioner and invested with the seal of Forward General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, replacing Zhu Rong as garrison commander of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, Kai was made vice commissioner and given the seal of Forward General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, replacing Zhu Rong as commander of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 時中國人自塞外脫歸者，令悉送京師，俟親屬赴領。

translations.literal: At the time Chinese who had escaped from beyond the passes were all ordered sent to the capital to await relatives coming to claim them.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese who had escaped from beyond the passes were then all sent to the capital to await relatives who would claim them.

sentences.zh: 凱言遠道往來，恐致失所，阻遠人慕歸心。

translations.literal: Kai argued that the long journey back and forth might cause them to lose their way and would obstruct the desire of distant folk to return in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Kai argued that the long journey might cause them to go astray and would discourage distant people from wishing to return.

sentences.zh: 乃更令有馬及少壯者送京師，余得自便。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was changed: those with horses and in their prime were sent to the capital; the rest were left to their own convenience.
translations.idiomatic: The rule was changed: only those with horses and in their prime were sent to the capital; the rest were left free.

sentences.zh: 敵掠西山，凱擊敗之，盡得所掠者，降敕褒勉。

translations.literal: When the enemy raided Xishan, Kai struck and defeated them, recovering all who had been taken; an imperial edict of praise and encouragement was issued.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy raided Xishan, Kai defeated them and recovered all who had been taken; an edict of praise was issued.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗遣使造舟松花江招諸部。

translations.literal: The emperor once dispatched envoys to build boats on the Songhua River to summon the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once sent envoys to build boats on the Songhua River to summon the tribes.

sentences.zh: 地遠，軍民轉輸大困，多逃亡。

translations.literal: The region was remote; transport by troops and civilians caused great hardship, and many fled.
translations.idiomatic: The region was remote; transport by troops and civilians caused great hardship, and many fled.

sentences.zh: 會有警，凱力請罷其役，而逃軍入海西諸部者已五百余人。

translations.literal: When an alarm arose, Kai urgently petitioned to halt the labor; already more than 500 deserters had gone among the tribes west of the sea.
translations.idiomatic: When an alarm arose, Kai urgently asked that the labor be stopped; already more than five hundred deserters had fled to the tribes west of the sea.

sentences.zh: 既而造舟役復興，中官阮堯民、都指揮劉清等董之。

translations.literal: Later the boat-building labor was revived, supervised by the eunuch Ruan Yaomin and Regional Commander Liu Qing and others.
translations.idiomatic: Later the boat-building labor was revived under the eunuch Ruan Yaomin, Regional Commander Liu Qing, and others.

sentences.zh: 多不法，致激變。

translations.literal: Many acted unlawfully, provoking uprising.
translations.idiomatic: Many acted unlawfully and provoked revolt.

sentences.zh: 凱劾堯民等，下之吏。

translations.literal: Kai impeached Yaomin and the others, who were handed over to the judicial authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Kai impeached Yaomin and the others, who were handed over to the courts.

sentences.zh: 英宗登極，進都督同知，上言邊情八事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, Kai was promoted to Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief and memorialized eight matters concerning frontier conditions.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, Kai was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief and memorialized eight points on frontier conditions.

sentences.zh: 請厚恤死事者家，益官吏折俸鈔，歲給軍士冬衣布棉，軍中口糧芻粟如舊制，且召商實邊。

translations.literal: He requested generous relief for families of those who died in service, increases to officials' salary deductions in paper notes, annual issue of winter clothing, cotton, and cloth to the troops, rations of grain and fodder within the army according to the old regulations, and additionally summoning merchants to supply the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He asked generous relief for families of the fallen, higher salary deductions in paper notes for officials, annual winter clothing and cotton for the troops, army grain and fodder rations under the old rules, and merchants summoned to supply the frontier.

sentences.zh: 俱允行。

translations.literal: All were approved for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為兵部尚書王驥所劾。

translations.literal: Before long he was impeached by Minister of War Wang Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was impeached by Minister of War Wang Ji.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知凱賢，令凱自陳。

translations.literal: The court knew Kai was capable and ordered him to state his own case.
translations.idiomatic: The court knew Kai was capable and ordered him to state his own case.

sentences.zh: 並諭廷臣，文武官有罪得實始奏，誣者罪不貸。

translations.literal: At the same time the civil and military officials were instructed that charges must be substantiated before memorializing guilt, and false accusers would not be spared punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were also told that civil and military charges must be proved before memorializing guilt, and false accusers would not be spared.

sentences.zh: 凱由是得行其誌。

translations.literal: Kai was thereby able to carry out his aims.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was thus able to carry out his aims.

sentences.zh: 正統三年十二月有疾，命醫馳視，未至而卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year of Zhengtong he fell ill; physicians were ordered to hurry to attend him, but before they arrived he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the third year of Zhengtong he fell ill; physicians were ordered to hurry to him, but before they arrived he died.

sentences.zh: 凱性剛毅，饒智略，馭眾嚴而有恩。

translations.literal: Kai was firm and resolute by nature, rich in stratagem, strict yet kind toward those he commanded.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was firm and resolute by nature, full of stratagem, strict yet kind toward those he led.

sentences.zh: 在遼東三十余年，威惠並行，邊務修飭。

translations.literal: For more than thirty years in Liaodong, awe and kindness went hand in hand, and frontier affairs were kept in good order.
translations.idiomatic: For more than thirty years in Liaodong he combined awe with kindness, and frontier affairs were kept in good order.

sentences.zh: 前後守東陲者，曹義外皆莫及。

translations.literal: Of those who had guarded the eastern marches before and after, none could match him except Cao Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Of those who had guarded the eastern marches before and after, none could match him except Cao Yi.

sentences.zh: 義，字敬方，儀真人。

translations.literal: Yi, courtesy name Jingfang, was a man of Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, styled Jingfang, was a native of Yizhen.

sentences.zh: 以燕山左衛指揮僉事累功至都督僉事，副凱守遼東。

translations.literal: Starting as vice commander of the Yan Mountains Left Guard, through accumulated merit he reached vice commissioner-in-chief and served as deputy to Kai in guarding Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: From vice commander of the Yan Mountains Left Guard he rose through merit to vice commissioner-in-chief and served under Wu Kai guarding Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 凱卒，代為總兵官。

translations.literal: When Kai died, he replaced him as supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Kai died, he succeeded him as supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 凱，名將，義承其後，廉介有守，遼人安之。

translations.literal: Kai was a famed general; Yi succeeded him, was incorruptible and principled, and the people of Liaodong were reassured by him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kai had been a famed general; Cao Yi followed in his stead, upright and principled, and the people of Liaodong were at ease under him.

sentences.zh: 兀良哈犯廣寧前屯，詔切責，命王翺往飭軍務，劾義死罪。

translations.literal: The Uriankhai invaded Guangning and Qiantun; an edict sharply rebuked him, ordered Wang Ao to go regulate military affairs, and impeached Yi on a capital charge.
translations.idiomatic: When the Uriankhai raided Guangning and Qiantun, the court sharply rebuked him, sent Wang Ao to tighten military discipline, and impeached Cao Yi on a capital charge.

sentences.zh: 頃之，義獲犯邊孛臺等，詔戮於市。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, Yi captured the border violators Botai and others; an edict ordered them executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Cao Yi captured the raiders Botai and others; the court ordered them executed in public.

sentences.zh: 自是義數與兀良哈戰。

translations.literal: From then on Yi fought the Uriankhai on several occasions.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Cao Yi fought the Uriankhai repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 正統九年，會朱勇軍夾擊。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhengtong, he joined Zhu Yong's army in a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhengtong he joined Zhu Yong's force in a pincer attack.

sentences.zh: 斬獲多，進都督同知，累官左都督。

translations.literal: Many were beheaded and captured; he was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief and through successive offices reached left commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He took many heads and captives, was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief, and eventually rose to left commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 義在邊二十年，無赫赫功，然能謹守邊陲。

translations.literal: Yi spent twenty years on the frontier without brilliant feats, yet he could guard the borderlands diligently.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yi spent twenty years on the frontier without spectacular victories, yet he kept the marches secure.

sentences.zh: 其麾下施聚、焦禮等皆至大將。

translations.literal: Under his command, Shi Ju, Jiao Li, and others all rose to senior generals.
translations.idiomatic: Men under him such as Shi Ju and Jiao Li all rose to senior general rank.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，特封義豐潤伯，聚亦封懷柔伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong restored the throne, Yi was specially enfeoffed as Marquis of Fengrun, and Ju was also enfeoffed as Marquis of Huairou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong regained the throne, Cao Yi was specially made Marquis of Fengrun, and Shi Ju was also enfeoffed as Marquis of Huairou.

sentences.zh: 居四年，義卒，贈侯，謚莊武。

translations.literal: After four years Yi died; he was posthumously granted the rank of marquis and given the posthumous name Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later Cao Yi died; he was posthumously made a marquis with the temple name Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 繼室李氏殉，詔旌之。

translations.literal: His stepwife Lady Li died in martyrdom; an edict honored her.
translations.idiomatic: His stepwife Lady Li took her own life in devotion; the court ordered her publicly commended.

sentences.zh: 施聚，其先沙漠人，居順天通州。

translations.literal: Shi Ju — his ancestors were desert people; the family lived in Tongzhou, Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ju's forebears came from the desert; his family lived in Tongzhou, Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 父忠為金吾右衛指揮使，從北征，陣歿，聚嗣職。

translations.literal: His father Zhong was regional commander of the Jinyu Right Guard; he joined the northern expedition, died in battle, and Ju succeeded to the post.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhong commanded the Jinyu Right Guard, joined a northern campaign, and fell in battle; Shi Ju inherited the post.

sentences.zh: 宣德中，備禦遼東，累擢都指揮同知。

translations.literal: During Xuande he served in defense of Liaodong and through successive promotions reached assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuande reign he defended Liaodong and was promoted to assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 以義薦，進都指揮使。

translations.literal: On Yi's recommendation he was advanced to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: On Cao Yi's recommendation he was promoted to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 義與兀良哈戰，聚皆從。

translations.literal: Whenever Yi fought the Uriankhai, Ju always followed.
translations.idiomatic: In every fight Cao Yi waged against the Uriankhai, Shi Ju went with him.

sentences.zh: 也先逼京師，景帝詔聚與焦禮俱入衛。

translations.literal: When Esen pressed the capital, Emperor Jingdi ordered Ju and Jiao Li together to enter and guard it.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen threatened the capital, Emperor Jingdi ordered Shi Ju and Jiao Li to march to its defense.

sentences.zh: 聚慟哭，即日引兵西。

translations.literal: Ju wept bitterly and the same day led his troops westward.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ju broke down weeping and that very day marched west with his troops.

sentences.zh: 部下進牛酒，聚揮之曰：「天子安在？

translations.literal: Subordinates offered cattle and wine; Ju waved them off and said: "Where is the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: When his men brought cattle and wine, Shi Ju waved them away and cried: "Where is the emperor?

sentences.zh: 吾屬何心饗此！

translations.literal: What heart have we to enjoy this!
translations.idiomatic: How can we bear to feast on this!

sentences.zh: 」比至，寇已退，乃還。

translations.literal: " By the time they arrived, the invaders had already withdrawn, and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: " When they reached the capital the enemy had already withdrawn, and they turned back.

sentences.zh: 聚以勇敢稱，官至左都督。

translations.literal: Ju was famed for bravery and reached the office of left commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ju was known for courage and rose to left commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 值英宗推恩，得封伯。

translations.literal: When Yingzong extended grace, he received enfeoffment as a marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong extended favor, he was enfeoffed as a marquis.

sentences.zh: 後義二年卒，贈侯，謚威靖。

translations.literal: He died two years after Yi, was posthumously granted marquis, and given the posthumous name Weijing.
translations.idiomatic: He died two years after Cao Yi, was posthumously made a marquis, and given the temple name Weijing.

sentences.zh: 義三傳至棟，聚四傳至瑾，吏部皆言不當復襲，世宗特許之。

translations.literal: Yi's title passed three generations to Dong; Ju's passed four generations to Jin; the Ministry of Personnel all said hereditary succession should not be restored, but Emperor Shizong specially permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Cao line passed three generations to Dong; the Shi line passed four to Jin; the Ministry of Personnel ruled that neither should inherit, but Emperor Shizong granted special permission.

sentences.zh: 傳爵至明亡。

translations.literal: The titles were transmitted until the Ming perished.
translations.idiomatic: Both lines held their peerages until the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 許貴，字用和，江都人，永新伯成子也。

translations.literal: Xu Gui, courtesy name Yonghe, was a man of Jiangdu, son of the Marquis of Yongxin, Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gui, styled Yonghe, was a native of Jiangdu and son of Marquis Cheng of Yongxin.

sentences.zh: 襲職為羽林左衛指揮使。

translations.literal: He inherited the post as regional commander of the Yulin Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited command of the Yulin Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 安鄉伯張安舉貴將才，試騎射及策皆最，擢署都指揮同知。

translations.literal: Zhang An, Marquis of Anxiang, recommended Gui's generalship; in trials of horsemanship, archery, and strategy he ranked first, and was promoted to acting assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Zhang An of Anxiang recommended Xu Gui's martial talent; he topped trials in riding, archery, and strategy and was made acting assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 尋以武進伯朱冕薦擢山西行都司，督操大同諸衛士馬。

translations.literal: Soon on the recommendation of Zhu Mian, Marquis of Wujin, he was promoted to the Shanxi Regional Military Commission and supervised drill of troops and horses of the guards at Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon on Marquis Zhu Mian of Wujin's recommendation he was raised to the Shanxi Regional Military Commission to drill the Datong garrison troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 正統末，守備大同西路。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengtong he served as garrison commander of Datong's western route.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Zhengtong reign he commanded the western Datong garrison.

sentences.zh: 也先入寇，從石亨戰陽和後口，敗績，貴力戰得還。

translations.literal: When Esen invaded, he followed Shi Heng in fighting at the rear pass of Yanghe; the battle was lost, but Gui fought hard and managed to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen invaded, he fought with Shi Heng at Yanghe Rear Pass; though the army was defeated, Xu Gui fought fiercely and got back alive.

sentences.zh: 英宗北狩，邊城悉殘破，大同當敵沖，人心尤恟懼。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was taken north on campaign, border cities were all ravaged; Datong stood in the enemy's path, and hearts were especially fearful and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yingzong was captured on the northern campaign, border cities lay in ruins; Datong stood directly in the enemy's path, and morale was especially shaken.

sentences.zh: 貴以忠義激戰士。

translations.literal: Gui roused the warriors with talk of loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gui stirred the troops with appeals to loyalty and duty.

sentences.zh: 敵來，擊敗之。

translations.literal: When the enemy came, he attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy came, he beat them back.

sentences.zh: 進都指揮使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年春，充右參將。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Jingtai, he served as right assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Jingtai 1 he was appointed right assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 敵寇威遠，追敗之浦州營，奪還所掠人畜。

translations.literal: The enemy raided Weiyuan; he pursued and defeated them at Puzhou Camp and recovered the people and livestock they had seized.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders hit Weiyuan, he pursued them to Puzhou Camp, routed them, and recaptured stolen people and livestock.

sentences.zh: 敵萬騎逼城下，禦卻之。

translations.literal: Ten thousand enemy horsemen pressed to the foot of the walls; he repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: When ten thousand enemy riders closed on the walls, he drove them off.

sentences.zh: 再遷都督同知。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He received a further promotion to assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 大同乏馬，命求民間，得八百余匹。

translations.literal: Datong lacked horses; he was ordered to seek them among the people and obtained more than eight hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Datong was short of horses; ordered to requisition them from civilians, he gathered more than eight hundred.

sentences.zh: 所司不給直，貴為請，乃予之。

translations.literal: The responsible offices did not pay fair price; Gui petitioned on their behalf, and payment was then given.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities refused full payment; Xu Gui petitioned for the sellers and they were finally compensated.

sentences.zh: 嘗募死士入賊壘，劫馬百余，悉畀戰士，士皆樂為用。

translations.literal: Once he recruited daredevils to enter the enemy stockade and seize more than a hundred horses, giving them all to the warriors, who were all glad to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: He once recruited daredevils to raid an enemy camp for more than a hundred horses and gave every one to his troops, who served him willingly.

sentences.zh: 分守中官韋力轉淫虐，眾莫敢言，貴劾奏之。

translations.literal: Wei Lizhuan, the eunuch holding divided garrison duty, was licentious and cruel; none dared speak, but Gui impeached and memorialized against him.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison eunuch Wei Lizhuan was brutal and corrupt; no one dared speak out, but Xu Gui impeached him.

sentences.zh: 三年，疾還京。

translations.literal: In the third year, ill, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he fell ill and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，命理左府事，尋調南京。

translations.literal: When Yingzong restored the throne, he was ordered to manage affairs of the Left Military Commission; soon he was transferred to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong regained the throne, he was put in charge of the Left Military Commission and soon transferred to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 松潘地雜番苗，密邇董卜韓胡，舊設參將一人。

translations.literal: Songpan's land mixed Fan and Miao peoples, lay close to Dongbuhankhu, and had formerly one assistant commander posted there.
translations.idiomatic: Songpan was home to mixed Fan and Miao peoples near Dongbuhankhu and had long had a single assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 天順五年，守臣告警，廷議設副總兵，以貴鎮守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianshun the local garrison reported alarm; court deliberation established a vice supreme commander post, with Gui to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 5 the garrison raised the alarm; the court created a vice supreme commander post and sent Xu Gui to hold it.

sentences.zh: 未抵鎮而山都掌蠻叛，詔便道先翦之。

translations.literal: Before he reached his post the Shanduzhang tribes rebelled; an edict ordered him by the direct route first to cut them down.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached his post the Shanduzhang tribes rebelled; he was ordered to take the direct route and suppress them first.

sentences.zh: 貴分兩哨直抵其巢，連破四十余寨。

translations.literal: Gui split into two columns that drove straight to their lair and in succession broke more than forty stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gui split his force into two columns, struck straight at their strongholds, and took more than forty stockades in succession.

sentences.zh: 斬首千一百級，生擒八百余人，余賊遠遁。

translations.literal: Heads cut numbered eleven hundred; more than eight hundred were captured alive; the remaining bandits fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: His men took eleven hundred heads, captured more than eight hundred alive, and the rest fled deep into the hills.

sentences.zh: 貴亦感嵐氣，未至松潘卒。

translations.literal: Gui also succumbed to miasma and died before reaching Songpan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gui too fell victim to the mountain miasma and died before reaching Songpan.

sentences.zh: 帝為輟朝一日，賜賻及祭葬如制。

translations.literal: The emperor suspended court for one day on his account and granted condolence gifts and sacrificial burial according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspended court for a day, and granted condolence payment and state funeral rites as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 子寧，字誌道。

translations.literal: His son Ning, courtesy name Zhidao.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu Ning, styled Zhidao.

sentences.zh: 正統末，自以舍人從軍有功，為錦衣千戶。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengtong, as a household attendant he followed the army with merit and was made a chiliarch of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Zhengtong reign he served as a household attendant in the field, earned merit, and was made a chiliarch of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 貴歿，嗣指揮使。

translations.literal: When Gui died, he succeeded as regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Gui died, he inherited the regional command.

sentences.zh: 用薦擢署都指揮僉事，守禦柴溝堡。

translations.literal: On recommendation he was promoted to acting vice commander-in-chief and defended Chaigou Fort.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation he was made acting vice commander-in-chief and posted to Chaigou Fort.

sentences.zh: 成化初，充大同遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: Early in Chenghua he served as mobile corps general of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chenghua reign he was appointed mobile corps general of Datong.

sentences.zh: 寇入犯，與同官秦傑等禦之小龍州澗，擒其右丞把禿等十一人。

translations.literal: When raiders invaded, together with colleagues such as Qin Jie he defended at Xiaolongzhou Ravine and captured their right vice minister Batu and eleven others.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders invaded, he and fellow officers including Qin Jie held them at Xiaolongzhou Ravine and captured eleven men including the enemy vice minister Batu.

sentences.zh: 改督宣府操練，移延綏。

translations.literal: He was reassigned to supervise drill at Xuanfu and transferred to Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to drill troops at Xuanfu, then transferred to Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 地逼河套，寇數入掠孤山堡。

translations.literal: The territory bordered the Ordos Loop; raiders often entered to plunder Gushan Fort.
translations.idiomatic: The post bordered the Ordos Loop, and raiders repeatedly struck Gushan Fort.

sentences.zh: 寧提孤軍奮擊之，三戰皆捷，寇渡河走。

translations.literal: Ning led a lone army and fought fiercely; three battles were all won, and the raiders crossed the river and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ning led a lone detachment in fierce fighting, won three engagements in a row, and drove the raiders back across the river.

sentences.zh: 明年復以三千騎入沙河墩，與總兵官房能禦之。

translations.literal: The next year they again entered with three thousand riders at Shahedun; together with supreme commander Fang Neng he repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: The next year three thousand horsemen raided Shahedun; he and supreme commander Fang Neng drove them off.

sentences.zh: 寇退，復掠康家岔。

translations.literal: The raiders withdrew, then plundered again at Kangjia Pass.
translations.idiomatic: After withdrawing, the raiders struck again at Kangjia Pass.

sentences.zh: 寧出塞百五十里，追與戰，獲馬牛羊千余而還。

translations.literal: Ning went beyond the pass one hundred fifty li, pursued and fought, and returned with more than a thousand horses, cattle, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ning pursued them a hundred and fifty li beyond the border, fought them, and returned with more than a thousand horses, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 時能守延綏，無將略，巡撫王銳請濟師。

translations.literal: At the time Neng held Yan-sui but lacked generalship; grand coordinator Wang Rui requested reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Neng held Yan-sui but lacked generalship; grand coordinator Wang Rui called for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 詔大同巡撫王越帥眾赴，越遣寧出西路。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Datong grand coordinator Wang Yue to lead the host thither; Yue dispatched Ning by the western route.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Datong grand coordinator Wang Yue to march with reinforcements; Wang Yue sent Xu Ning by the western route.

sentences.zh: 破敵黎家澗，進都指揮同知。

translations.literal: He defeated the enemy at Lijia Ravine and was promoted to assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He routed the enemy at Lijia Ravine and was promoted to assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 復遣寧與都指揮陳輝追寇，獲馬騾六百。

translations.literal: Ning was again dispatched with regional commander Chen Hui to pursue the raiders and seized six hundred horses and mules.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ning was again sent with regional commander Chen Hui in pursuit and captured six hundred horses and mules.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以阿羅出復入河套，頻擾邊，命越與朱永禦，而以寧才，擢都督僉事，佩靖虜副將軍印，代能充總兵官。

translations.literal: The court, because Alaq had re-entered the Ordos Loop and frequently harassed the border, ordered Yue and Zhu Yong to defend, and because of Ning's talent promoted him to vice commissioner-in-chief, invested him with the seal of Vice General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and replaced Neng as supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: Because Alaq had reoccupied the Ordos and was raiding the frontier, the court put Wang Yue and Zhu Yong in command of defenses and, judging Xu Ning's ability, made him vice commissioner-in-chief with the seal of Vice General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, replacing Fang Neng as supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 寧起世胄，不十年至大將，同列推讓不及，父友多隸部下，亦不以為驟。

translations.literal: Ning rose from a hereditary house; in less than ten years he reached senior general rank; colleagues could not defer fast enough; many of his father's friends served under him, yet they did not think the rise too sudden.
translations.idiomatic: Born to a military family, Xu Ning reached senior general rank in under ten years; colleagues struggled to keep pace, and though many of his father's friends served under him, none thought the promotion too sudden.

sentences.zh: 逾月，寇大入，永遣寧及遊擊孫鉞禦之。

translations.literal: After a month raiders invaded in force; Yong sent Ning and mobile corps commander Sun Yue to repel them.
translations.idiomatic: A month later a major raid struck; Zhu Yong sent Xu Ning and mobile corps commander Sun Yue to meet it.

sentences.zh: 至波羅堡，相持三日夜，寇乃解去。

translations.literal: At Boluo Fort they faced each other three days and nights before the raiders withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At Boluo Fort they held the enemy for three days and nights before the raiders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 亡失多，寧以力戰得出，卒被賞。

translations.literal: Many were lost; Ning fought his way out by force and in the end was rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Casualties were heavy, but Xu Ning fought his way free and was rewarded nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 至冬，賊入安邊，寧追擊有功。

translations.literal: By winter raiders entered Anbian; Ning pursued and struck with merit.
translations.idiomatic: That winter raiders entered Anbian; Xu Ning pursued them with success.

sentences.zh: 七年又與諸將孫鉞、祝雄等敗寇於滉忽都河，璽書褒獎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he again joined generals Sun Yue, Zhu Xiong, and others in defeating raiders at the Huanghudu River; an imperial letter praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he and generals Sun Yue and Zhu Xiong routed raiders at Huanghudu River; the emperor sent a letter of commendation.

sentences.zh: 迤北開元王把哈孛羅屢欲降，內懼朝廷見罪，外畏河羅出仇之，徬徨不決。

translations.literal: To the far north, Kaoyuan Prince Baohaluo often wished to surrender, inwardly fearing punishment from the court, outwardly fearing vengeance from Heluochu, and wavered unable to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Far to the north, Kaoyuan Prince Baohaluo wished repeatedly to surrender but feared the court's wrath at home and Heluochu's revenge abroad, and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 寧請撫慰以固其心，卒降之。

translations.literal: Ning requested pacification and reassurance to fix his heart, and in the end received his surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ning urged conciliation to win him over, and Baohaluo finally submitted.

sentences.zh: 明年，參將錢亮敗績於師婆澗。

translations.literal: The next year Assistant Commander Qian Liang suffered defeat at Shipojian.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Assistant Commander Qian Liang was defeated at Shipo Ravine.

sentences.zh: 士卒死者十三四，寧與越等俱被劾。

translations.literal: Of the soldiers three or four in ten died; Ning, Yue, and others were all impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Three or four soldiers in ten were killed; Xu Ning, Wang Yue, and others were all impeached.

sentences.zh: 帝不罪。

translations.literal: The emperor did not punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor declined to punish them.

sentences.zh: 時滿都魯等屢犯延綏，寧帥鎮兵力戰。

translations.literal: At the time Mandulu and others repeatedly violated Yan-sui; Ning led the garrison troops in fierce battle.
translations.idiomatic: Mandulu and others were raiding Yan-sui repeatedly; Xu Ning led the garrison in hard fighting.

sentences.zh: 寇不得誌，乃出西路，直犯環慶、固原。

translations.literal: The raiders could not achieve their aim and went out by the western route, striking straight at Huanqing and Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to gain their objective, the raiders swung west and struck Huanqing and Guyuan directly.

sentences.zh: 寧將輕騎夜襲之鴨子湖，奪馬畜而還。

translations.literal: Ning led light cavalry in a night raid at Yazihu and returned having seized horses and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ning led light cavalry in a night strike at Yazi Lake and returned with seized horses and livestock.

sentences.zh: 又明年，寇入榆林澗，與巡撫余子俊敗之。

translations.literal: Again the next year raiders entered Yulin Ravine; together with grand coordinator Yu Zijun he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The year after, raiders entered Yulin Ravine; he and grand coordinator Yu Zijun defeated them.

sentences.zh: 滿都魯等大入西路，留其家紅鹽池。

translations.literal: Mandulu and others entered deeply by the western route, leaving their families at Hongyan Pool.
translations.idiomatic: Mandulu's force plunged deep along the western route, leaving families at Red Salt Pool.

sentences.zh: 越乘間與寧及宣府將周玉襲破其巢。

translations.literal: Yue seized the interval together with Ning and Xuanfu general Zhou Yu to raid and smash their lair.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue seized the opening and, with Xu Ning and Xuanfu general Zhou Yu, stormed their base.

sentences.zh: 進署都督同知。

translations.literal: He was advanced to acting assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 與子俊築邊墻，增營堡，寇患少衰。

translations.literal: Together with Zijun he built border walls and increased camps and forts; raider trouble somewhat declined.
translations.idiomatic: Working with Yu Zijun he built border walls and added forts, and frontier raids eased.

sentences.zh: 十八年，寇分數道入，寧蹙之邊墻，獲級百二十。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year raiders entered in several columns; Ning pressed them to the border wall and took one hundred twenty heads.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year raiders came by several routes; Xu Ning drove them to the border wall and took a hundred and twenty heads.

sentences.zh: 予實授。

translations.literal: He was granted the appointment in full.
translations.idiomatic: His acting commission was made permanent.

sentences.zh: 時越方鎮大同，命寧與易鎮。

translations.literal: At the time Yue was garrisoning Datong; Ning was ordered to exchange posts with him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue was then commanding Datong; Xu Ning was ordered to swap posts with him.

sentences.zh: 至則與鎮守太監汪直不協。

translations.literal: When he arrived he did not get along with the garrison eunuch Wang Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: On taking up his new command he clashed with garrison eunuch Wang Zhi.

sentences.zh: 巡撫郭鏜以聞，調直南京。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Guo Tang reported this; Zhi was transferred to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Guo Tang memorialized the court, and Wang Zhi was transferred to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 小王子大入。

translations.literal: The Lesser Prince invaded in force.
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser Prince launched a major invasion.

sentences.zh: 寧知敵勢盛，欲持重俟隙，乃斂兵守，而別遣將劉寧、董升與周璽相犄角。

translations.literal: Ning knew the enemy strength was great, wished to hold his weight and await an opening, and therefore drew in troops to guard, while separately dispatching generals Liu Ning, Dong Sheng, and Zhou Xi to support one another like horns of a stag.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the enemy's strength, Xu Ning chose to hold back and wait for an opening; he kept his main force in defense while sending generals Liu Ning, Dong Sheng, and Zhou Xi to coordinate from separate positions.

sentences.zh: 寇大掠，焚代王別堡。

translations.literal: The raiders plundered heavily and burned the Prince of Dai's secondary fort.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders pillaged widely and burned the Prince of Dai's outlying fort.

sentences.zh: 王趣戰，使眾哭於轅門。

translations.literal: The prince urged battle and had the crowd weep at the camp gate.
translations.idiomatic: The prince pressed for action and ordered troops to weep before the camp gate in protest.

sentences.zh: 寧憤，與鏜等營城外。

translations.literal: Ning was angry and, together with Tang and the others, encamped outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ning, furious, went out with Guo Tang and the others to encamp beyond the walls.

sentences.zh: 寇以十余人為誘，太監蔡新部騎馳擊。

translations.literal: The raiders used more than ten men as bait; eunuch Cai Xin's mounted detachment galloped to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders sent a dozen men as decoys, and eunuch Cai Xin's cavalry raced out to attack.

sentences.zh: 寧將士爭赴之，遇伏大敗，死者千余人。

translations.literal: Ning's officers and soldiers all rushed to join the fight, met an ambush, and suffered a great defeat; more than a thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ning's troops all rushed forward and walked into an ambush; more than a thousand were killed in the rout.

sentences.zh: 寧奔夏米莊，鏜、新馳入城。

translations.literal: Ning fled to Xiami Village; Tang and Xin galloped into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ning fled to Xiami Village while Guo Tang and Cai Xin raced back inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 會璽等來援，寇乃退。

translations.literal: When Xi and the others arrived in relief, the raiders then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xi and others then came to reinforce them, and the raiders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 寧還，陣亡家婦子號呼詬詈，擲以瓦礫，寧大喪氣。

translations.literal: When Ning returned, the wives and children of the slain wailed and cursed him and threw tiles and stones at him; Ning was greatly dispirited.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Ning came back, widows and orphans of the fallen shouted curses at him and pelted him with rubble; he was utterly crushed.

sentences.zh: 已而寇復入，劉寧、宋澄、莊鑒等禦之。

translations.literal: Before long the raiders entered again; Liu Ning, Song Cheng, Zhuang Jian, and others defended against them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the raiders returned; Liu Ning, Song Cheng, Zhuang Jian, and others held them off.

sentences.zh: 十戰，少利，寇退。

translations.literal: After ten battles they gained little advantage, and the raiders withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They fought ten engagements with only slight gain before the raiders pulled back.

sentences.zh: 寧等掩其敗，更以捷聞。

translations.literal: Ning and the others concealed their defeat and instead reported victory.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ning and his colleagues covered up the defeat and reported a victory instead.

sentences.zh: 巡按程春震發之，與鏜、新俱下獄。

translations.literal: Investigating censor Cheng Chunzhen exposed it, and together with Tang and Xin they were all imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Cheng Chunzhen exposed the fraud, and Xu Ning, Guo Tang, and Cai Xin were all thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 鏜降六官，新以初任降三官，寧降指揮同知閑住。

translations.literal: Tang was demoted six ranks; Xin, because he had just taken office, was demoted three ranks; Ning was demoted to assistant commander with the same nominal rank and placed in idle residence.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tang was stripped of six ranks; Cai Xin, as a newly appointed officer, lost three; Xu Ning was reduced to assistant commander with nominal rank and sent into inactive service.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，用薦署都指揮使，分領操練。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi reign, on recommendation he was appointed acting regional commander and put in charge of drill and training.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign he was recommended for acting regional commander and assigned to lead training exercises.

sentences.zh: 十一年十二月卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the eleventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month of the eleventh year.

sentences.zh: 贈都督僉事。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 寧束發從軍，大小百十余戰，身被二十七創。

translations.literal: Ning bound his hair and entered the army; in more than a hundred battles large and small he received twenty-seven wounds on his body.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ning had taken up arms in youth; over more than a hundred engagements, large and small, he bore twenty-seven wounds.

sentences.zh: 性沈毅，守官廉，待士有恩，不屑幹進。

translations.literal: By nature he was deep and resolute; in office he was incorrupt, treated officers with kindness, and disdained pushing for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Steady and resolute by nature, he served honestly, treated his men generously, and scorned self-promotion.

sentences.zh: 劉寧、神英、李杲皆出麾下。

translations.literal: Liu Ning, Shen Ying, and Li Gao all came from under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ning, Shen Ying, and Li Gao all rose from his command.

sentences.zh: 子泰，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Tai has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tai has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 周賢，滁人，襲宣府前衛千戶。

translations.literal: Zhou Xian was a native of Chu and inherited the chiliarch post of the Xuanfu Forward Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xian, a native of Chu, inherited the chiliarchship of the Xuanfu Forward Guard.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，累功至都指揮僉事，守備西貓兒峪，助副總兵孫安守石八城。

translations.literal: At the opening of the Jingtai reign, through accumulated merit he rose to vice regional commander, garrisoned Ximao'er Pass, and assisted deputy commander-in-chief Sun An in holding Shibacheng.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingtai reign he rose through merit to vice regional commander, garrisoned Ximao'er Pass, and helped deputy commander Sun An hold Shibacheng.

sentences.zh: 尋充右參將，代安鎮守。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he served as right assistant commander and replaced An in garrison command.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made right assistant commander and took over Sun An's garrison command.

sentences.zh: 兀良哈入寇，總兵官過興令宣府副將楊信及賢合擊。

translations.literal: The Uriangqai invaded; commander-in-chief Guo Xing ordered Xuanfu deputy general Yang Xin and Xian to join in a combined attack.
translations.idiomatic: When the Uriangqai raided, commander-in-chief Guo Xing ordered Xuanfu deputy Yang Xin and Zhou Xian to strike together.

sentences.zh: 賢不俟信，徑擊敗之。

translations.literal: Xian did not wait for Xin and went straight to attack and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xian did not wait for Yang Xin and attacked on his own, routing the enemy.

sentences.zh: 信被劾，都御史李秉言信緩師，賢亦棄約。

translations.literal: Xin was impeached; censor-in-chief Li Bing said Xin had delayed the army, and Xian had also abandoned the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xin was impeached; censor-in-chief Li Bing charged that he had held back the force, and Zhou Xian was also accused of breaking their agreement.

sentences.zh: 帝兩宥之。

translations.literal: The emperor pardoned them both.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned them both.

sentences.zh: 天順初，總兵官楊能奏賢擢都督僉事。

translations.literal: At the opening of the Tianshun reign, commander-in-chief Yang Neng memorialized that Xian be promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshun reign, commander-in-chief Yang Neng recommended Zhou Xian for promotion to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 寇駐塞下，能檄賢與大軍會，失期，征下獄。

translations.literal: The raiders halted below the pass; Neng ordered Xian to join the main army, but he missed the deadline and was summoned and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: With raiders camped below the frontier, Yang Neng ordered Zhou Xian to rendezvous with the main force; he missed the deadline and was arrested.

sentences.zh: 以故官赴寧夏，隸定遠伯石彪。

translations.literal: With his former rank he went to Ningxia and served under Dingyuan Earl Shi Biao.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Ningxia at his former rank and served under Dingyuan Earl Shi Biao.

sentences.zh: 寇二萬騎入安邊營。

translations.literal: Twenty thousand mounted raiders entered Anbian Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty thousand mounted raiders struck Anbian Camp.

sentences.zh: 彪率賢等擊之，連戰皆捷，追至野馬澗、半坡墩，寇大敗。

translations.literal: Biao led Xian and the others to attack them; in successive battles they were all victorious, pursued them to Yema Stream and Banpodun, and the raiders suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Biao led Zhou Xian and others against them, winning battle after battle and chasing the enemy to Yema Stream and Banpodun in a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 而賢追不已，中流矢卒。

translations.literal: But Xian pursued without stopping, was struck by a flying arrow, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xian pressed the pursuit relentlessly, was struck by an arrow, and died.

sentences.zh: 詔贈都督同知。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously ennobled him as assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 賢初下吏，自以不復用，及得釋，感激誓死報，竟如其誌。

translations.literal: When Xian was first sent to the magistrates he believed he would never be employed again; once released he was moved to swear he would repay with his life, and in the end he fulfilled that vow.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Xian was first imprisoned he thought he would never serve again; after his release he vowed to repay the throne with his life, and in the end he did.

sentences.zh: 子玉，字廷璧，當嗣指揮使。

translations.literal: His son Yu, styled Tingbi, was to inherit the post of regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhou Yu, styled Tingbi, was heir to the regional commandership.

sentences.zh: 以父死事，超二官為萬全都司都指揮同知，督理屯田。

translations.literal: Because his father died in service, he was promoted two ranks beyond regular advancement to assistant regional commander of the Wanquan Regional Military Commission and put in charge of garrison farming.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had died in battle, he was promoted two ranks to assistant regional commander of the Wanquan commission and assigned to oversee garrison farming.

sentences.zh: 進都指揮使，充宣府遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to regional commander and appointed mobile-strike general of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to regional commander and served as mobile-strike general of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 成化九年，會昌侯孫繼宗等奉詔舉將才，玉為首。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chenghua, Marquis of Huichang Sun Jizong and others, by imperial order, recommended commanders of talent; Yu was ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Chenghua, Marquis of Huichang Sun Jizong and others were ordered to recommend military talent; Zhou Yu headed the list.

sentences.zh: 詔率所部援延綏，從王越襲紅鹽池。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to lead his troops to relieve Yan-sui and, following Wang Yue, raid Hongyan Pool.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to lead his troops to reinforce Yan-sui and, under Wang Yue, strike Red Salt Pool.

sentences.zh: 進署都督僉事，還守宣府。

translations.literal: He was advanced to acting vice commissioner-in-chief and returned to guard Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting vice commissioner-in-chief and returned to hold Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 寇入馬營、赤城，擊敗之。

translations.literal: Raiders entered Maying and Chicheng; he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders entered Maying and Chicheng, he drove them off.

sentences.zh: 兵部言宣府諸大帥無功，玉所部三千人能追敵出境，請加一秩酬其勞，乃予實授。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War stated that the great commanders of Xuanfu had achieved no merit, while Yu's three thousand men could pursue the enemy beyond the border; it requested one additional rank to reward his labor, and he was then granted the appointment in full.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War noted that Xuanfu's senior commanders had accomplished nothing while Zhou Yu's three thousand men had chased the enemy beyond the frontier; it asked that he be raised one rank in reward, and his commission was made permanent.

sentences.zh: 尋充宣府副總兵。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he served as deputy commander-in-chief of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made deputy commander of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 十三年佩征朔將軍印，鎮宣府。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he wore the seal of General Who Conquers the North and garrisoned Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he took the seal of General Who Conquers the North and commanded Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 破敵紅崖，追奔至水磨灣。

translations.literal: He defeated the enemy at Hongya and pursued the fleeing force to Shuimowan.
translations.idiomatic: He broke the enemy at Red Cliff and chased them to Shuimowan.

sentences.zh: 進署都督同知。

translations.literal: He was advanced to acting assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十七年五月，寇復入犯，參將吳儼、少監崖榮追出塞，至赤把都，為所遮，兵分為三，皆被圍。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year the raiders invaded again; assistant commander Wu Yan and junior eunuch Ya Rong pursued them beyond the pass to Chibadu, were intercepted, their troops split into three groups, and all were surrounded.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year raiders struck again; Assistant Commander Wu Yan and junior eunuch Ya Rong pursued them beyond the frontier to Chibadu, were cut off, and all three divisions were encircled.

sentences.zh: 儼、榮走據北山，因甚。

translations.literal: Yan and Rong fled and held North Mountain, and were greatly distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yan and Ya Rong fled to hold North Mountain and were in dire straits.

sentences.zh: 守備張澄率兵進，力戰，解二圍。

translations.literal: Garrison commander Zhang Cheng led troops forward, fought fiercely, and broke two encirclements.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commander Zhang Cheng advanced, fought hard, and lifted two of the sieges.

sentences.zh: 抵北山下，儼、榮已夜遁。

translations.literal: When he reached the foot of North Mountain, Yan and Rong had already fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached North Mountain, Wu Yan and Ya Rong had already slipped away under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 澄拔其眾而還，死者過半。

translations.literal: Cheng extricated his force and returned; more than half had died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cheng fought his way out with the survivors, but more than half his men were dead.

sentences.zh: 澄所部七百人，亦多戰死。

translations.literal: Of the seven hundred men under Cheng's command, many also died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Of Zhang Cheng's seven hundred men, many also fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 詔錄澄功，治儼等罪。

translations.literal: An edict recorded Cheng's merit and punished Yan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The court recognized Zhang Cheng's achievement and punished Wu Yan and the others.

sentences.zh: 玉先以葛谷堡、赤城頻受掠，凡三被論，至是復以節制不嚴見劾。

translations.literal: Yu had earlier been criticized three times because Gegu Fort and Chicheng were repeatedly plundered; now he was again impeached for lax command.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu had already been censured three times over repeated raids on Gegu Fort and Chicheng; now he was impeached again for failing to keep discipline.

sentences.zh: 帝皆置不問。

translations.literal: The emperor set all of this aside and did not inquire into it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor let every charge drop.

sentences.zh: 十九年，小王子犯大同。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the Lesser Prince violated Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the Lesser Prince attacked Datong.

sentences.zh: 敗總兵官許寧。

translations.literal: He defeated commander-in-chief Xu Ning.
translations.idiomatic: He routed commander-in-chief Xu Ning.

sentences.zh: 入順聖川大掠，以六千騎寇宣府。

translations.literal: He entered Shunsheng River and plundered heavily, then with six thousand horsemen raided Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: After pillaging Shunsheng River valley, he turned six thousand horsemen against Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 玉將二千人前行，巡撫秦纮兵繼進，至白腰山擊敗之。

translations.literal: Yu led two thousand men forward; grand coordinator Qin Hong's troops followed, and at Baiyao Mountain they defeated the raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu led two thousand men ahead while grand coordinator Qin Hong's force came up behind; together they defeated the raiders at Baiyao Mountain.

sentences.zh: 指揮曹洪邀擊至西陽河，都指揮孫成亦敗寇七馬房。

translations.literal: Commander Cao Hong intercepted and pursued them to Xiyang River; regional commander Sun Cheng also defeated the raiders at Qimafang.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Cao Hong cut them off and chased them to Xiyang River, while regional commander Sun Cheng also routed them at Qimafang.

sentences.zh: 時寇乘勝，氣甚銳，竟為玉等所挫，一時稱其功。

translations.literal: At the time the raiders were riding victory and their spirit was very sharp, yet in the end they were checked by Yu and the others, and for a time his merit was praised.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders were riding a wave of victories and fighting with fierce momentum, yet Zhou Yu and his colleagues turned them back, and his achievement was widely praised.

sentences.zh: 未幾，寇復入，玉伏兵敗之。

translations.literal: Before long the raiders entered again; Yu set an ambush and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the raiders returned; Zhou Yu laid an ambush and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 朱永至大同，復會玉軍擊敗之鵓鴿峪。

translations.literal: Zhu Yong arrived at Datong, joined Yu's army again, and defeated the raiders at Bogeyu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yong reached Datong, joined Zhou Yu's force, and defeated the raiders at Bogeyu.

sentences.zh: 進署右都督。

translations.literal: He was advanced to acting right commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting right commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 余子俊築邊墻，玉不為力，且與纮不相能。

translations.literal: Yu Zijun built border walls; Yu did not exert himself and moreover did not get along with Hong.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Zijun built the border wall, Zhou Yu gave little help and clashed with Qin Hong besides.

sentences.zh: 子俊惡之，奏與寧夏神英易鎮。

translations.literal: Zijun disliked him and memorialized that he exchange garrisons with Shen Ying of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zijun turned against him and had him transferred to swap posts with Shen Ying in Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 久之，復移鎮甘肅。

translations.literal: After a long time he was again transferred to garrison Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred again to command Gansu.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嗣位，實授右都督。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong succeeded to the throne, Yu was granted the right commander-in-chiefship in full.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong took the throne, Zhou Yu received a permanent commission as right commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 玉督邊墻工峻急，部卒張伏興等以瓦石投之。

translations.literal: Yu supervised border-wall work with harsh urgency; his subordinate soldiers Zhang Fuxing and others threw tiles and stones at him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu drove the border-wall labor relentlessly, and his troops Zhang Fuxing and others pelted him with stones.

sentences.zh: 兵部言，悍卒漸不可長，遂戮伏興，戍其黨。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War stated that unruly soldiers must not be indulged; Fuxing was therefore executed and his followers were sent to frontier garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War argued that mutinous soldiers could not be tolerated; Zhang Fuxing was executed and his accomplices were banished to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 土魯番貢獅子，願獻還哈密成及金印，贖所留使者。

translations.literal: Turpan presented a lion and wished to return Hami ruler and the gold seal to redeem the envoys it had detained.
translations.idiomatic: Turpan sent a lion as tribute and offered to restore the Hami ruler and the gold seal in exchange for detained envoys.

sentences.zh: 玉為之奏，帝命與巡撫王繼經畫。

translations.literal: Yu memorialized on their behalf; the emperor ordered him to plan the matter together with grand coordinator Wang Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu memorialized on the proposal, and the emperor ordered him to work out the arrangement with grand coordinator Wang Ji.

sentences.zh: 既果來歸，玉等皆受賚。

translations.literal: When they did indeed return, Yu and the others all received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys did return, Zhou Yu and his colleagues were all rewarded.

sentences.zh: 七年，病歸，尋卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he fell ill and returned home, and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he fell ill, went home, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 謚武僖。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Wuxi, "Martial and Joyful."

sentences.zh: 玉初為偏裨，及鎮宣府，甚有名。

translations.literal: Yu at first served as a junior officer; when he garrisoned Xuanfu he was greatly renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu began as a junior officer, but when he commanded Xuanfu he won great renown.

sentences.zh: 後蒞甘肅，部下屢失事，又侵屯田。

translations.literal: Later, when he took up office in Gansu, his subordinates repeatedly met with mishaps, and he also encroached on garrison farmland.
translations.idiomatic: Later in Gansu his subordinates suffered repeated failures, and he himself encroached on garrison lands.

sentences.zh: 死後事發，子襲職，降二等。

translations.literal: After his death the matter came to light; his son inherited the post but was demoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The abuses came to light after his death; his son inherited the family post but was demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 歐信，嗣世職金吾右衛指揮使。

translations.literal: Ōu Xin inherited the hereditary post of regional commander of the Jinyou Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Ōu Xin inherited the hereditary commandership of the Jinyou Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年以廣東破賊功，擢都指揮同知。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingtai, for merit in defeating bandits in Guangdong, he was promoted to assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jingtai he was promoted to assistant regional commander for defeating bandits in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 已，命守備白羊口，遷大寧都指揮使。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was ordered to garrison Baiyang Pass and was transferred to regional commander of Daning.
translations.idiomatic: He was then assigned to garrison Baiyang Pass and transferred to regional commander of Daning.

sentences.zh: 天順初，以都督僉事充參將，守備廣東雷、廉諸府。

translations.literal: At the opening of the Tianshun reign, as vice commissioner-in-chief he served as assistant commander and garrisoned Leizhou, Lianzhou, and other prefectures of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshun reign he served as assistant commander at vice commissioner rank, garrisoning Leizhou, Lianzhou, and other Guangdong prefectures.

sentences.zh: 巡撫葉盛薦其廉勇。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Ye Sheng recommended him for integrity and courage.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Ye Sheng praised his integrity and bravery.

sentences.zh: 進都督同知，代副總兵翁信。

translations.literal: He was advanced to assistant commissioner-in-chief and replaced deputy commander-in-chief Weng Xin.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief and replaced deputy commander Weng Xin.

sentences.zh: 兩廣瑤僮陷開建，殺官吏，帝趣進兵。

translations.literal: Yao and Zhuang of the Two Guangs seized Kaijian, killed officials, and the emperor urgently ordered troops forward.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Zhuang raiders in the Two Guangs overran Kaijian and killed officials; the emperor ordered an immediate advance.

sentences.zh: 信破賊化州之馬裏村，再破之石城，擊斬海南衛反者邵瑄。

translations.literal: Xin defeated the bandits at Mali Village in Huazhou, defeated them again at Shicheng, and struck down and beheaded the rebel of Hainan Guard, Shao Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ōu Xin routed the rebels at Mali Village in Huazhou, defeated them again at Shicheng, and killed Shao Xuan, mutineer of Hainan Guard.

sentences.zh: 時所在盜群起，將吏不能定。

translations.literal: At the time bandit groups rose everywhere, and officers could not pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit bands were rising everywhere, and local commanders could not restore order.

sentences.zh: 廣西參將範信守潯、梧，瑤盡在境內，陰納瑤賂，縱使越境流劫，約毋犯己。

translations.literal: Guangxi assistant commander Fan Xin guarded Xunzhou and Wuzhou; the Yao were all within his territory, and he secretly accepted Yao bribes, allowing them to cross the border to raid and plunder on the understanding that they would not violate his own jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi assistant commander Fan Xin held Xunzhou and Wuzhou while Yao bands remained inside his territory; he secretly took their bribes and let them cross the border to raid elsewhere on condition they leave his posts alone.

sentences.zh: 於是雷、廉、高、肇悉被寇。

translations.literal: Thereupon Leizhou, Lianzhou, Gaozhou, and Zhaoqing were all raided.
translations.idiomatic: Leizhou, Lianzhou, Gaozhou, and Zhaoqing were all ravaged as a result.

sentences.zh: 帝命廣西總兵官陳涇及信合剿。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Guangxi commander-in-chief Chen Jing and Xin to join in a combined suppression.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Guangxi commander Chen Jing and Ōu Xin to suppress the rebels jointly.

sentences.zh: 時有斬馘，而賊勢不衰，朝廷猶倚範信。

translations.literal: At the time there were decapitations taken, but the bandit strength did not decline, and the court still relied on Fan Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Heads were taken, yet the rebels' strength did not break, and the court still leaned on Fan Xin.

sentences.zh: 會涇以罪征，乃擢範信都督僉事充副總兵，鎮廣東，而命信佩征蠻將軍印，代涇鎮廣西。

translations.literal: When Jing was summoned on a charge of crime, Fan Xin was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief and made deputy commander-in-chief garrisoning Guangdong, while Xin was ordered to wear the seal of General Who Conquers the Barbarians and replace Jing in garrisoning Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Jing was recalled on criminal charges, Fan Xin was promoted to vice commissioner and made deputy commander of Guangdong, while Ōu Xin was given the seal of General Who Conquers the Barbarians and replaced Chen Jing in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 成化元年，賊掠英德諸縣，信討斬五百余人，奪還人口。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chenghua bandits plundered the counties of Yingde; Xin pursued and beheaded more than five hundred men and recovered the people who had been seized.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chenghua rebels raided the counties around Yingde; Ōu Xin killed more than five hundred of them and recovered captives.

sentences.zh: 韓雍督師，令信等分五哨，攻破大藤峽。

translations.literal: Han Yong supervised the army and ordered Xin and the others to divide into five columns and storm Dateng Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yong took overall command and sent Ōu Xin and others in five columns to break Dateng Gorge.

sentences.zh: 已而余賊復入潯州，信被劾獲宥，召還，理前府事。

translations.literal: Before long remnant bandits entered Xunzhou again; Xin was impeached but pardoned, recalled, and put in charge of his former prefectural duties.
translations.idiomatic: Remnant rebels later re-entered Xunzhou; Ōu Xin was impeached but pardoned, recalled, and restored to his former prefectural duties.

sentences.zh: 七年春，充總兵官，鎮守遼東，累敗福余三衛。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year he served as commander-in-chief, garrisoned Liaodong, and repeatedly defeated the Three Guards of Fuyu.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year he became commander-in-chief of Liaodong and repeatedly defeated the Three Fuyu Guards.

sentences.zh: 言者謂信已老，請召還。

translations.literal: Memorialists said Xin was already old and requested that he be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued that Ōu Xin was too old and asked that he be recalled.

sentences.zh: 巡撫彭誼奏：「官軍耆老五千余人，皆言信忠謹有謀勇，累立戰功，威鎮邊陲。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Peng Yi memorialized: "More than five thousand veteran soldiers of the garrison all say that Xin is loyal, prudent, resourceful, and brave, has repeatedly won battlefield merit, and whose prestige secures the frontier borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Peng Yi memorialized: "More than five thousand veteran garrison soldiers all attest that Ōu Xin is loyal, prudent, resourceful, and brave, has won repeated battlefield honors, and whose authority holds the frontier firm.

sentences.zh: 年六旬，騎射勝壯士，不宜召回。

translations.literal: Though sixty years of age, in mounted archery he surpasses strong men; he should not be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Though sixty years old, he still outshoots younger men from horseback; he should not be recalled.

sentences.zh: 」乃留鎮如故。

translations.literal: " Therefore he was left in garrison command as before.
translations.idiomatic: " The court therefore kept him in command as before.

sentences.zh: 久之，陳鉞代誼。

translations.literal: After a long time Chen Yue replaced Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In time Chen Yue replaced Peng Yi.

sentences.zh: 鉞貪功，信不能違，十四年為巡按王崇之所劾。

translations.literal: Yue was greedy for merit, and Xin could not refuse; in the fourteenth year he was impeached by touring censor Wang Chongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yue was greedy for credit, and Ōu Xin could not refuse him; in the fourteenth year Ōu Xin was impeached by touring censor Wang Chongzhi.

sentences.zh: 其冬，乃召歸。

translations.literal: That winter he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 尋遣中官汪直等往按，直右鉞，歸罪信等。

translations.literal: Soon eunuchs Wang Zhi and others were sent to investigate; Zhi favored Yue and laid the blame on Xin and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon sent the eunuch Wang Zhi and others to investigate; Wang Zhi sided with Chen Yue and placed the blame on Ōu Xin and his associates.

sentences.zh: 下獄，鐫一官閑住，飲恨而卒。

translations.literal: He was imprisoned, reduced one rank and made to live in retirement, and died nursing resentment.
