translations.idiomatic: He was thrown into prison, stripped of one rank and ordered to live in retirement, and died consumed by bitterness.

sentences.zh: 範信既徙廣東，賊勢愈盛，劫掠不止，乃語人曰：「今賊仍犯廣東，亦我遣之耶。

translations.literal: After Fan Xin was transferred to Guangdong, bandit strength grew ever greater and raids did not cease; he said to people: "The bandits are still raiding Guangdong—is that because I sent them there?
translations.idiomatic: Once Fan Xin was moved to Guangdong, rebel strength only grew and raids never stopped; he told others, "The rebels are still attacking Guangdong—did I send them there myself?

sentences.zh: 」而是時都督顏彪佩征夷將軍印，討賊久無功，濫殺良民報捷。

translations.literal: " At that time regional commander Yan Biao wore the seal of General Who Conquers the Barbarians; though he campaigned long against the bandits without success, he indiscriminately killed common people to report victory.
translations.idiomatic: " At the same time Regional Commander Yan Biao held the seal of General Who Conquers the Barbarians; he had campaigned against the rebels for a long time without success, yet slaughtered innocent civilians to claim victories.

sentences.zh: 嶺南人鹹疾之。

translations.literal: The people of Lingnan all despised him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Lingnan loathed him.

sentences.zh: 王璽，太原左衛指揮同知也。

translations.literal: Wang Xi was assistant regional commander of Taiyuan Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi was assistant regional commander of the Taiyuan Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 成化初，擢署都指揮僉事，守禦黃河七墅。

translations.literal: At the opening of Chenghua he was promoted to acting assistant regional commander and garrisoned Qishi on the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chenghua reign he was promoted to acting assistant regional commander and posted to garrison Qishi on the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 巡撫李侃薦於朝。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Li Kan recommended him to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Li Kan recommended him at court.

sentences.zh: 阿魯出寇延綏，命充遊擊將軍赴援，戰孤山堡，敗之。

translations.literal: When Aru invaded Yan-sui, he was ordered to serve as mobile corps general to go to the rescue; he fought at Gushan Fort and defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Aru raided Yan-sui, he was appointed mobile corps general to reinforce the frontier; he fought at Gushan Fort and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 寇再入，戰漫天嶺、劉宗塢及漫塔、水磨川，皆有功。

translations.literal: When the raiders entered again, he fought at Mantian Ridge, Liuzong'ao, Mantu, and Shuimochuan, each time with merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders returned, he fought at Mantian Ridge, Liuzong'ao, Mantu, and Shuimochuan, winning credit in every engagement.

sentences.zh: 進都指揮同知，充副總兵，鎮守寧夏。

translations.literal: He was advanced to assistant regional commander, made deputy commander-in-chief, and garrisoned Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant regional commander, made deputy commander, and garrisoned Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 九年以將才與周玉同薦。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he and Zhou Yu were jointly recommended for military talent.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he and Zhou Yu were jointly recommended for command ability.

sentences.zh: 十二年擢署都督僉事，充總兵官，鎮守甘肅。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to acting vice commissioner-in-chief, made commander-in-chief, and garrisoned Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was promoted to acting vice commissioner-in-chief, made commander-in-chief, and posted to garrison Gansu.

sentences.zh: 黃河以西，自莊浪抵肅州南山，其外番人阿吉等二十九族所居也。

translations.literal: West of the Yellow River, from Zhuanglang to the southern mountains of Suzhou, beyond lay the lands where the foreign tribesmen Aji and twenty-nine other clans lived.
translations.idiomatic: West of the Yellow River, from Zhuanglang to the southern mountains of Suzhou, lay the territory of the foreign tribes led by Aji and twenty-eight other clans.

sentences.zh: 洪武間，立石畫界，約樵牧毋越疆，歲久湮廢，諸番往往闌入，而中國無賴人又潛與交通為邊患。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign stone markers were erected to mark the border, with the agreement that woodcutters and herders would not cross the line; after many years this sank into disuse, and the various tribes often trespassed, while ruffians from within China also secretly trafficked with them, creating border troubles.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongwu era border stones were set up to mark the frontier and woodcutters and herders were forbidden to cross; over time the markers fell into ruin, tribes often slipped across the line, and Chinese outlaws secretly traded with them, turning the border into a chronic trouble spot.

sentences.zh: 璽請「復畫疆域，召集諸番，諭以界石廢，恐官軍欺淩諸部，今復立之，聽界外駐牧，互市則入關。

translations.literal: Xi memorialized: "Restore the delineation of territory, summon the various tribes, and explain to them that since the border stones fell into disuse they fear the garrison troops will bully their tribes; now the markers are to be re-erected, and they may pasture beyond the line, but for trade they must enter the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi memorialized: "Let us redraw the border, summon the tribes, and tell them that with the boundary stones gone they fear harassment by garrison troops; restore the markers, allow them to pasture beyond the line, and require them to enter the passes only for trade.

sentences.zh: 如此，番人必聽命，可潛消他日憂。

translations.literal: In this way the tribes will surely obey, and future troubles may be quietly averted.
translations.idiomatic: If we do this, the tribes will surely submit, and future troubles can be quietly averted.

sentences.zh: 」帝稱善，從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised the plan and approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor praised the proposal and approved it.

sentences.zh: 十七年進署都督同知。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to acting assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to acting assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時璽以都督僉事為總兵官，而魯鑒以署都督同知為參將，璽恐難於節制，乞解兵柄，故有是命。

translations.literal: At the time Xi served as commander-in-chief at vice commissioner rank while Lu Jian served as assistant commander at acting assistant commissioner rank; Xi feared difficulty in commanding him and asked to relinquish military authority, hence this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Xi held command as a vice commissioner while Lu Jian served as assistant commander at acting assistant commissioner rank; Wang Xi feared he could not control him and asked to surrender military authority, which led to this promotion.

sentences.zh: 初，哈密為土魯番所擾，使其將牙蘭守之。

translations.literal: Initially Hami was harassed by Turfan, which sent its general Yalan to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Hami had been harassed by Turfan, which placed its general Yalan in charge of the city.

sentences.zh: 都督罕慎寄居苦峪口，近赤斤、罕東，數相攻，罕慎勢窮無援。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Han Shen took refuge at Kuyukou, close to Chijin and Handong; they repeatedly attacked one another, and Han Shen's forces were exhausted and had no support.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Han Shen had taken refuge at Kuyukou near Chijin and Handong; the three sides repeatedly clashed, and Han Shen's position collapsed for lack of support.

sentences.zh: 朝議敕璽築城苦峪，別立哈密衛以居之。

translations.literal: The court resolved to order Xi to build a city at Kuyu and establish a separate Hami Guard in which to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: The court decided to order Wang Xi to build a city at Kuyu and establish a separate Hami Guard to resettle them.

sentences.zh: 璽遣諜者間牙蘭。

translations.literal: Xi sent spies to sow discord with Yalan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi sent spies to undermine Yalan.

sentences.zh: 牙蘭不聽，得其所羈掠九十余人以歸，具悉虛實。

translations.literal: Yalan would not listen, but they recovered more than ninety people he had seized and returned with full knowledge of conditions there.
translations.idiomatic: Yalan paid no heed, but the spies recovered more than ninety captives he had taken and returned with a full picture of enemy strength.

sentences.zh: 十七年召集赤斤、罕東將士，犒以牛酒，令助罕慎。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he gathered the officers and soldiers of Chijin and Handong, rewarded them with cattle and wine, and ordered them to aid Han Shen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he summoned the officers and troops of Chijin and Handong, feasted them with cattle and wine, and ordered them to support Han Shen.

sentences.zh: 罕慎合二衛兵，夜襲哈密及剌木等八城，遂復其地，仍令罕慎居之。

translations.literal: Han Shen combined the troops of the two guards, made a night raid on Hami and eight cities including Laimu, recovered the territory, and Han Shen was again put in residence there.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shen combined the forces of the two guards and launched a night attack on Hami and eight cities including Laimu; he recovered the territory and was restored to residence there.

sentences.zh: 事聞，獎勞，賚金幣。

translations.literal: When the report arrived, rewards were given and gold and silks bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court, he was rewarded and given gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 已，罕東入寇，璽禦卻之，請興師以討。

translations.literal: Before long Handong invaded; Xi repelled them and requested that an expedition be launched against them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Handong raided the frontier; Wang Xi drove them back and asked that troops be raised to punish them.

sentences.zh: 帝念其常助罕慎，第遣使責諭。

translations.literal: The emperor, remembering that they had often aided Han Shen, only sent envoys to rebuke them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, recalling that they had often helped Han Shen, sent envoys only to rebuke them.

sentences.zh: 明年，北寇殺哨卒，璽率參將李俊及赤斤兵擊之於狼心山、黑河西，多所斬獲。

translations.literal: The next year northern raiders killed sentry soldiers; Xi led Assistant Commander Li Jun and Chijin troops to strike them at Langxin Mountain and west of the Hei River, killing and capturing many.
translations.idiomatic: The next year northern raiders killed frontier sentries; Wang Xi led Assistant Commander Li Jun and Chijin troops against them at Langxin Mountain and west of the Hei River, killing and capturing many.

sentences.zh: 二十年移鎮大同。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was transferred to garrison Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was transferred to command at Datong.

sentences.zh: 璽有復哈密功，官不進，陳於朝，乃實授都督同知。

translations.literal: Though Xi had merit in recovering Hami, his rank was not advanced; after he stated this to the court, he was formally appointed assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Though Wang Xi had merit in recovering Hami, his rank had not advanced; after he appealed at court, he was formally appointed assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 璽習韜略，諳文事，勇而有謀。

translations.literal: Xi was versed in strategy, skilled in civil affairs, brave and resourceful.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi knew strategy, was literate in civil affairs, and was brave as well as shrewd.

sentences.zh: 廷臣多稱之。

translations.literal: Court officials widely praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials widely praised him.

sentences.zh: 在邊二十余年，為番人所憚。

translations.literal: He served on the frontier more than twenty years and was feared by the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He spent more than twenty years on the frontier and was feared by the tribes.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 賜祭葬，贈恤有加。

translations.literal: An imperial sacrifice and funeral were granted, with added posthumous honors and relief.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him an imperial sacrifice and funeral, with enhanced posthumous honors and relief.

sentences.zh: 魯鑒，其先西大通人。

translations.literal: Lu Jian's ancestors were people of the western Datong region.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jian's ancestors came from western Datong.

sentences.zh: 祖阿失都鞏卜失加，明初率部落歸附，太祖授為百夫長，俾統所部居莊浪。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ashidu Gongbushijia at the opening of the dynasty led his tribe to submit; the Taizu appointed him centurion and ordered him to lead his people to settle at Zhuanglang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ashidu Gongbushijia submitted with his tribe at the dynasty's founding; the Taizu made him a centurion and settled his people at Zhuanglang.

sentences.zh: 傳子失加，累官莊浪衛指揮同知。

translations.literal: The post passed to his son Shijia, who rose through the ranks to assistant regional commander of Zhuanglang Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The post passed to his son Shijia, who rose to assistant regional commander of Zhuanglang Guard.

sentences.zh: 正統末，鑒嗣父職。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhengtong reign Jian inherited his father's post.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Zhengtong reign Lu Jian inherited his father's command.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢署都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: After some time he was promoted to acting assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was promoted to acting assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 成化四年，固原滿四反，鑒以土兵千人從征。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chenghua Man Si revolted at Guyuan; Lu Jian took a thousand native troops to join the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chenghua Man Si rebelled at Guyuan; Lu Jian led a thousand native troops on campaign.

sentences.zh: 諸軍圍石城，日挑戰，鑒出則先驅，入則殿後，最為賊所憚。

translations.literal: When the armies besieged Shicheng and challenged daily, whenever Jian went out he led the van and when he entered he brought up the rear; the rebels feared him above all.
translations.idiomatic: As the armies besieged Shicheng and fought daily, Lu Jian led the van on the advance and guarded the rear on withdrawal; the rebels feared him most of all.

sentences.zh: 賊平，進署都督同知。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was promoted to acting assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were suppressed, he was promoted to acting assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 尋充左參將，分守莊浪。

translations.literal: Soon he was made left assistant commander with divided command over Zhuanglang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made left assistant commander with divided command over Zhuanglang.

sentences.zh: 命其子麟為百戶，統治土軍。

translations.literal: His son Lin was appointed centurion to command the native troops.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lin was appointed centurion to command the native troops.

sentences.zh: 十七年坐寇入境，戴罪立功。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year because raiders entered the territory he was ordered to redeem guilt through meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, after raiders crossed the border, he was ordered to redeem his fault through meritorious service.

sentences.zh: 尋充左副總兵，協守甘肅。

translations.literal: Soon he was made left deputy commander-in-chief to assist in garrisoning Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made left deputy commander to assist in garrisoning Gansu.

sentences.zh: 寇犯永昌。

translations.literal: Raiders violated Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders struck Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 被劾。

translations.literal: He was impeached.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached.

sentences.zh: 鑒疏辨，第停其俸兩月。

translations.literal: Jian memorialized in his defense, and only his salary was suspended for two months.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jian memorialized in his defense, and only his salary was suspended for two months.

sentences.zh: 俄命充總兵官，鎮守延綏。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed commander-in-chief garrisoning Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed commander-in-chief of Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 自陳往功，予實授。

translations.literal: Having stated his past merit, he was formally appointed.
translations.idiomatic: After citing his past service, he received formal appointment.

sentences.zh: 孝宗立，得疾，致仕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong came to the throne, he fell ill and retired.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne, Lu Jian fell ill and retired.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，命麟襲指揮使，加都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Early in Hongzhi Lin was ordered to inherit the post of regional commander and was given the additional rank of assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi, Lin was ordered to inherit the regional commandership and was given the additional rank of assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 已，進同知，充甘肅遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was advanced to assistant regional commander and made mobile corps general of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to assistant regional commander and made mobile corps general of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 魯氏世守西陲，有捍禦功，至鑒官益顯，其世業益大，而所部土軍生齒又日盛。

translations.literal: The Lu clan had for generations held the western frontier with meritorious service in defense; by Lu Jian's time their official standing grew ever more prominent and their hereditary enterprise ever greater, while the native troops under their command also multiplied day by day.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the Lu clan had held the western frontier with distinguished defensive service; under Lu Jian their official standing grew ever higher and their hereditary command ever larger, while the native troops under them also multiplied steadily.

sentences.zh: 麟既移甘肅，帝以土軍非鑒不能治，特起治之，且命有司建坊旌其世績。

translations.literal: After Lin was transferred to Gansu, the emperor felt the native troops could not be governed without Lu Jian and specially recalled him to manage them, and also ordered the relevant offices to erect a commemorative arch honoring the clan's generations of achievement.
translations.idiomatic: After Lin was transferred to Gansu, the emperor decided the native troops could be governed only by Lu Jian and specially recalled him; he also ordered officials to erect a commemorative arch honoring the clan's generations of service.

sentences.zh: 鑒乃條上邊務四事，多議行。

translations.literal: Lu Jian then memorialized four items concerning frontier affairs in sequence; most were discussed and adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jian then submitted four proposals on frontier affairs in order; most were debated and adopted.

sentences.zh: 鑒有材勇，遇敵輒冒矢石，數被傷不為沮，故能積功至大將。

translations.literal: Lu Jian had ability and courage; whenever he met the enemy he would expose himself to arrows and stones, and though wounded many times he was not deterred, thus accumulating merit until he reached the rank of great general.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jian was talented and brave; in battle he always exposed himself to arrow and stone fire, and though wounded many times he never faltered, accumulating merit until he rose to great general.

sentences.zh: 十五年以舊創疾發，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year an old wound flared up and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year an old wound reopened and he died.

sentences.zh: 贈右都督，賜恤如制。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Right Regional Commander, and relief was granted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Right Regional Commander, and relief was granted by regulation.

sentences.zh: 時麟已由甘肅參將擢左副總兵，豪健如其父，而恭順不如。

translations.literal: At the time Lin had been promoted from Gansu assistant commander to left deputy commander-in-chief; he was as bold and strong as his father but not as deferential.
translations.idiomatic: By then Lin had risen from Gansu assistant commander to left deputy commander; he was as bold and strong as his father but less obedient.

sentences.zh: 先為遊擊時，寇入永昌，失律，委罪副將陶禎。

translations.literal: Earlier, when he was mobile corps general, raiders entered Yongchang; he violated military law and shifted blame to Deputy Commander Tao Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while serving as mobile corps general, he broke discipline when raiders entered Yongchang and shifted blame to Deputy Commander Tao Zhen.

sentences.zh: 下御史按，當戍邊，但貶一秩，遊擊如故。

translations.literal: Censors were sent to investigate; he was sentenced to frontier service but was only reduced one rank and kept his post as mobile corps general.
translations.idiomatic: Censors were dispatched to investigate; he was liable to frontier service but was only reduced one rank and kept his mobile corps post.

sentences.zh: 暨為副將，調韋州禦寇。

translations.literal: When he became deputy commander he was transferred to Weizhou to repel raiders.
translations.idiomatic: After he became deputy commander he was transferred to Weizhou to repel raiders.

sentences.zh: 寇大入不能擊，遣都指揮楊琳邀之孔壩溝。

translations.literal: When raiders poured in en masse he could not strike them; he sent Regional Commander Yang Lin to intercept them at Kongbagou.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders poured in he failed to engage them and sent Regional Commander Yang Lin to intercept them at Kongbagou.

sentences.zh: 琳大敗，不救，連被劾。

translations.literal: Yang Lin was heavily defeated, and Lin did not rescue him; he was repeatedly impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Lin was routed, and Lin did not go to his aid; Lin was impeached repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 麟自訴，止停俸二月。

translations.literal: Lin pleaded in his own defense, and only his salary was suspended for two months.
translations.idiomatic: Lin appealed in his own defense and was punished with only two months' suspended salary.

sentences.zh: 時已授麟子經官，令約束土軍。

translations.literal: At the time Lin's son Jing had already been given an official post and ordered to discipline the native troops.
translations.idiomatic: By then Lin's son Jing had already received an official post and been ordered to discipline the native troops.

sentences.zh: 而麟奏經幼，土人不受要束，乞歸治之。

translations.literal: But Lin memorialized that Jing was young and the native people would not accept his control, and requested to return to manage them himself.
translations.idiomatic: But Lin memorialized that Jing was too young and the native troops would not obey him, and asked to return home to manage them himself.

sentences.zh: 不俟報，徑歸。

translations.literal: Without waiting for a reply he went home directly.
translations.idiomatic: Without waiting for a reply he went home at once.

sentences.zh: 帝用劉大夏言，從其請。

translations.literal: The emperor, heeding Liu Daxia, granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, following Liu Daxia's advice, granted his request.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，甘肅巡撫畢亨薦經及麟謀勇，令率所部協戰守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong came to the throne, Gansu grand coordinator Bi Heng recommended Jing and Lin for planning and courage and ordered them to lead their troops in joint defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne, Gansu grand coordinator Bi Heng recommended Jing and Lin for strategy and courage and ordered them to lead their troops in joint defense.

sentences.zh: 正德二年，經既襲指揮使，自陳嘗隨父有功，乃以為都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde, after Jing inherited the regional commandership, he stated that he had followed his father in service with merit and was therefore made assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengde, after Jing inherited the regional commandership, he cited service at his father's side and was made assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 未幾，麟卒，贈都督僉事。

translations.literal: Before long Lin died and was posthumously made vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Lin died and was posthumously made vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 賜祭葬。

translations.literal: An imperial sacrifice and funeral were granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him an imperial sacrifice and funeral.

sentences.zh: 故事，都指揮無恤典，以經乞，破例予之。

translations.literal: By precedent regional commanders received no relief rites; at Jing's request an exception was made.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent regional commanders were not entitled to relief rites; at Jing's request an exception was made.

sentences.zh: 經積戰功，再遷都指揮使充左參將，分守莊浪。

translations.literal: Jing accumulated battlefield merit, was twice promoted to regional commander and made left assistant commander with divided command over Zhuanglang.
translations.idiomatic: Jing accumulated battlefield merit, was promoted twice to regional commander, and made left assistant commander with divided command over Zhuanglang.

sentences.zh: 復自陳功閥，兵部執不可。

translations.literal: He again stated his record of merit, but the Ministry of War held firm that it would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: He again cited his record of merit, but the Ministry of War refused.

sentences.zh: 帝特命為署都督僉事。

translations.literal: The emperor specially ordered him appointed acting vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor specially ordered him appointed acting vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，乞休。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong came to the throne, he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 巡撫許鳳翔言經力戰被創，疾行愈，且世將敢戰，知名異域，今邊患棘，不宜聽其去。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Xu Fengxiang stated that Jing had fought hard and been wounded, that though ill he was recovering, that as a hereditary commander famed abroad for daring in battle, and that with frontier troubles now acute he should not be allowed to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Xu Fengxiang argued that Jing had fought hard and been wounded, that though ill he was recovering, that as a hereditary commander famed beyond the frontier for daring in battle, and that with border troubles now acute he should not be allowed to leave.

sentences.zh: 帝乃諭留，且勞以銀幣。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered him retained and rewarded him with silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to stay and rewarded him with silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 尋充副總兵分守如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was again made deputy commander-in-chief with divided command as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as deputy commander with divided command as before.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖六年冬，以都督同知充總兵官，鎮守延綏。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year of Jiajing he was made commander-in-chief at assistant commissioner rank garrisoning Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixth year of Jiajing he was made commander-in-chief at assistant commissioner rank and posted to Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 大學士楊一清言：「經守莊浪二十余載，屢立戰功，其部下土軍非他人所能及。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Yang Yiqing said: "Jing has held Zhuanglang for more than twenty years and repeatedly won battlefield merit; the native troops under him are beyond what others can match.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yang Yiqing said: "Jing has held Zhuanglang for more than twenty years and won repeated battlefield honors; the native troops under him are unmatched.

sentences.zh: 雖其子瞻已為指揮僉事，奉命統轄，然年尚少。

translations.literal: Although his son Zhan is already assistant regional commander and has been ordered to take command, he is still young.
translations.idiomatic: Although his son Zhan is already assistant regional commander and has been ordered to take command, he is still young.

sentences.zh: 今陜西總兵官張鳳乃延綏世將，若調鳳延綏，而改經陜西，自可彈壓莊浪，無西顧患。

translations.literal: The present Shaanxi commander-in-chief Zhang Feng is a hereditary general of Yan-sui; if Zhang Feng is transferred to Yan-sui and Jing is moved to Shaanxi, he can himself keep Zhuanglang in hand without worrying about the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The present Shaanxi commander Zhang Feng is a hereditary Yan-sui general; if Zhang Feng is moved to Yan-sui and Jing to Shaanxi, Jing can hold Zhuanglang himself without fear for the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 」帝立從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor immediately approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor immediately approved.

sentences.zh: 居二年，竟以疾致仕。

translations.literal: After two years he finally retired on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he finally retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 久之，命瞻以本官守備山丹。

translations.literal: After some time Zhan was ordered to garrison Shandan at his existing rank.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Zhan was ordered to garrison Shandan at his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 經奏言：「自臣高祖後，世守茲土。

translations.literal: Jing memorialized: "Since my great-grandfather's time my family has held this land for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Jing memorialized: "Since my great-grandfather's time my family has held this land for generations.

sentences.zh: 今臣家居，瞻又移他鎮，土軍皇皇，不欲別附，若因此生他患，是隳先業而負世恩也，乞令守故業。

translations.literal: Now that I am at home and Zhan has been transferred to another garrison, the native troops are unsettled and unwilling to attach themselves elsewhere; if other troubles arise from this, it would ruin our ancestral enterprise and betray the dynasty's generations of favor—I beg that he be allowed to hold to our former post.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I am retired and Zhan has been moved to another post, the native troops are restless and unwilling to serve under anyone else; if this breeds new trouble, it will destroy our ancestral command and betray generations of imperial favor. I beg that he be allowed to keep our old post.

translations.literal: " Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，宣、大有警，詔經簡壯士五千赴援。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, when Xuanda and Datong raised alarms, the emperor ordered Jing to select five thousand strong men to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, when Xuanda and Datong came under alarm, the emperor ordered Jing to select five thousand strong men for relief.

sentences.zh: 至而邊患已息，乃遣還。

translations.literal: When he arrived the border trouble had already subsided, and he was sent back.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived the frontier crisis had already passed, and he was sent home.

sentences.zh: 以經力疾趨召，厚賚之。

translations.literal: Because Jing, though ill, hastened to answer the summons, he was richly rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had answered the summons despite illness, and the court rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 明年瞻卒。

translations.literal: The next year Zhan died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhan died.

sentences.zh: 經以次子及孫皆幼，請得自轄土軍。

translations.literal: Jing, because his second son and grandson were both young, requested permission to command the native troops himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's second son and grandson were both still young, so he asked to take personal command of the native troops.

sentences.zh: 詔許之。

translations.literal: An edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the request.

sentences.zh: 經驍勇，奉職寡過，繼祖父為大帥，保功名，稱良將。

translations.literal: Jing was fierce and brave, served his post with few faults, succeeded his grandfather as a great commander, preserved rank and fame, and was called a good general.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was fierce in battle and seldom faulted in office; succeeding his grandfather as commander-in-chief, he kept the family's honors and was reckoned a capable general.

sentences.zh: 三十五年卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirty-fifth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 賜恤如制。

translations.literal: Condolence grants were bestowed according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted the prescribed posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 劉寧，字世安，其先山陽人。

translations.literal: Liu Ning, styled Shi'an, was by origin from Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ning, courtesy name Shi'an, came from a Shanyang family.

sentences.zh: 襲世職，為永寧衛指揮使。

translations.literal: He inherited the hereditary post and served as regional commander of Yongning Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the family command and became regional commander of Yongning Guard.

sentences.zh: 勇敢善戰。

translations.literal: He was brave and skilled in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and a capable fighter.

sentences.zh: 自以冗散無所見，會延綏用兵，疏請效死。

translations.literal: He considered himself idle and without opportunity for distinction; when Yan-sui went to war, he memorialized asking to die in service.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling sidelined and without a chance to prove himself, he seized on the Yan-sui campaign to petition for a place where he could fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 尚書白圭許之。

translations.literal: Minister Bai Gui approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Bai Gui granted his request.

sentences.zh: 屢以功遷都指揮使，充宣府遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: Repeatedly for merit he was promoted to regional commander and made mobile corps general of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Merit after merit raised him to regional commander and mobile corps general of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 周璽，字廷玉，遷安人。

translations.literal: Zhou Xi, styled Tingyu, was a man of Qian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xi, courtesy name Tingyu, was from Qian'an.

sentences.zh: 嗣職為開平衛指揮使。

translations.literal: He succeeded to the post as regional commander of Kaiping Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the family post as regional commander of Kaiping Guard.

sentences.zh: 負氣習兵書，善騎射。

translations.literal: He was proud in temperament, studied military texts, and was skilled at horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Hot-tempered and studious in the art of war, he excelled at riding and shooting.

sentences.zh: 以征北功，擢署都指揮僉事充右參將，分守陽和，敕部兵三千訓肄聽調。

translations.literal: For northern campaign merit he was promoted and appointed acting assistant regional commander serving as right assistant commander with divided command over Yanghe; he was ordered to drill three thousand troops under him for dispatch on command.
translations.idiomatic: For his northern campaigns he was promoted to acting assistant regional commander and made right assistant commander with divided command over Yanghe, with orders to drill three thousand men for service at need.

sentences.zh: 成化十六年，從王越征威寧海子，累進都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Chenghua he followed Wang Yue in the campaign at Weining Lake and was repeatedly advanced to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 16 he followed Wang Yue against the enemy at Weining Lake and rose step by step to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 時邊寇無虛歲。

translations.literal: At that time border raiders came no year without incident.
translations.idiomatic: In those years the frontier saw raids every single year.

sentences.zh: 十八年分道入掠，璽與遊擊董昇戰黑石崖，寧戰塔兒山，皆有功。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year they entered in separate columns to plunder; Xi fought with mobile corps commander Dong Sheng at Heishi Cliff, and Ning fought at Ta'er Mountain—both won merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the raiders split into columns; Zhou Xi and mobile corps commander Dong Sheng fought at Heishi Cliff while Liu Ning fought at Ta'er Mountain, and all distinguished themselves.

sentences.zh: 璽進署都督僉事，遷大同副總兵。

translations.literal: Xi was advanced to acting vice commissioner-in-chief and transferred to deputy commander-in-chief of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xi was promoted to acting vice commissioner-in-chief and made deputy commander-in-chief of Datong.

sentences.zh: 寧進都督僉事，改左參將，分守陽和。

translations.literal: Ning was advanced to vice commissioner-in-chief, changed to left assistant commander, and given divided command over Yanghe.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ning was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief, reassigned as left assistant commander with divided command over Yanghe.

sentences.zh: 十九年秋，亦思馬因大入。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the nineteenth year Yisimayin invaded on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn of the nineteenth year Yisimayin launched a major invasion.

sentences.zh: 大同總兵官許寧分遣璽守懷仁，寧與董昇營西山，自將中軍，擊之夏米莊，敗績。

translations.literal: Datong commander-in-chief Xu Ning separately dispatched Xi to guard Huairen, sent Ning and Dong Sheng to camp at Xishan, and personally led the central army to strike them at Xiamizhuang, where he suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ning, commander-in-chief at Datong, posted Zhou Xi at Huairen, sent Liu Ning and Dong Sheng to encamp on Xishan, and led the central army himself against the enemy at Xiamizhuang—but was defeated.

sentences.zh: 寧、昇被圍數重，幾陷。

translations.literal: Ning and Sheng were surrounded layer upon layer and nearly lost.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ning and Dong Sheng were ringed by repeated encirclements and nearly overrun.

sentences.zh: 亟發巨炮擊之，敵多死，圍乃解。

translations.literal: They urgently fired great cannon at them; many of the enemy died, and the encirclement was then broken.
translations.idiomatic: They brought up heavy cannon in haste; many of the enemy fell, and the siege was broken.

sentences.zh: 璽聞中軍失利，亟還兵援。

translations.literal: Xi heard the central army had been defeated and urgently turned his troops back to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the central army had been beaten, Zhou Xi rushed back with his troops to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 夜遇敵，乘勝前，銳甚。

translations.literal: At night they encountered the enemy, who pressed forward on the momentum of victory and were very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: That night they met the enemy, who pressed their advantage and fought with fierce momentum.

sentences.zh: 璽厲將士曰：「今日有進無退！

translations.literal: Xi sternly told his officers and men: "Today there is advance and no retreat!
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xi rallied his men: "Today we advance—we do not retreat!

sentences.zh: 」大呼陷陣，敵少卻。

translations.literal: " He shouted and broke into the enemy line; the foe fell back somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: " With a great cry he charged the enemy line, and the raiders gave ground.

sentences.zh: 久之，短兵接。

translations.literal: After a long while they closed at close quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The fighting dragged on until they were locked in hand-to-hand combat.

sentences.zh: 臂中流矢，拔鏃戰益急，與子鵬及麾下壯士擊殺數十人。

translations.literal: An arrow struck his arm; he pulled out the head and fought all the more fiercely, and with his son Peng and valiant men under his command killed several tens of men.
translations.idiomatic: An arrow pierced his arm; he pulled out the shaft and fought harder still, and with his son Peng and his best warriors cut down dozens of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 會寧兵至，中軍潰卒亦稍集，敵乃退，許寧等亦還。

translations.literal: Just then Ning's troops arrived, the routed men of the central army also gradually gathered, the enemy then withdrew, and Xu Ning and the others also returned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ning's force arrived in time, scattered troops from the central army regrouped, and the enemy withdrew; Xu Ning and the rest also made their way back.

sentences.zh: 無何復入掠。

translations.literal: Before long they entered again to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the raiders struck again.

sentences.zh: 寧將兵三千，遇之聚落站西，連戰敗之。

translations.literal: Ning led three thousand troops, encountered them west of Juluo Station, and repeatedly fought and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ning led three thousand men, met them west of Juluo Station, and beat them in successive engagements.

sentences.zh: 復敗之白登、柳林，又追敗之小鵓鴿谷。

translations.literal: He again defeated them at Baideng and Liulin, and pursued and defeated them at Xiaoboguge Valley.
translations.idiomatic: He routed them again at Baideng and Liulin, then chased them down and defeated them at Xiaoboguge Valley.

sentences.zh: 而大同西路參將莊鑒亦邀其歸路，戰於牛心山，敵遂遁。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Datong western-route assistant commander Zhuang Jian also intercepted their line of retreat and fought at Niuxin Mountain; the enemy then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Jian, assistant commander on Datong's western route, also cut off their retreat and fought at Niuxin Mountain, and the enemy fled.

sentences.zh: 時諸將多失利，許寧以下獲罪，而璽以功予實授，寧超遷都督同知，莊鑒以所部無失亡，亦賚銀幣。

translations.literal: At that time many generals had suffered defeat; Xu Ning and those below him were punished, while Xi for merit was given substantive appointment, Ning was exceptionally promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief, and Zhuang Jian because his command suffered no losses or deaths was also rewarded with silver and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the commanders had been beaten; Xu Ning and his subordinates were punished. Zhou Xi received a substantive promotion for his service, Liu Ning was exceptionally raised to assistant commissioner-in-chief, and Zhuang Jian was rewarded with silver and silk because his troops had taken no losses.

sentences.zh: 鑒，遼東人。

translations.literal: Jian was a man of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Jian was from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 天順中，襲定遼右衛指揮使。

translations.literal: During Tianshun he inherited the post of regional commander of Dingliao Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianshun reign he inherited command of Dingliao Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 驍猛有膽決。

translations.literal: He was fierce and bold, with daring resolve.
translations.idiomatic: He was fierce in battle and resolute in judgment.

sentences.zh: 遇賊輒奮，數有功，累官都督僉事，掌左府。

translations.literal: Whenever he met bandits he roused himself; several times he won merit, rose through offices to vice commissioner-in-chief, and held the left bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He always fought with abandon when he met the enemy, won repeated honors, rose to vice commissioner-in-chief, and commanded the left bureau.

sentences.zh: 弘治十一年佩鎮朔將軍印，鎮宣府。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Hongzhi he wore the seal of Pacifier of the North and garrisoned Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 11 he took the seal of Pacifier of the North and was posted to Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 以才與大同總兵官張俊易鎮。

translations.literal: For his talent he exchanged garrisons with Datong commander-in-chief Zhang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: On account of his ability he exchanged posts with Datong commander-in-chief Zhang Jun.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎熊繡奏其經畫功，進都督同知。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Xiong Xiu memorialized his planning merit, and he was advanced to assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of War Xiong Xiu cited his strategic achievements, and he was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 璽尋以右副總兵分守代州，兼督偏頭諸關，而改寧左副總兵，協守大同。

translations.literal: Xi was soon made right deputy commander-in-chief with divided command over Daizhou, concurrently supervising the passes at Piantou and elsewhere, while Ning was changed to left deputy commander-in-chief to assist in guarding Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xi was soon made right deputy commander-in-chief with divided command over Daizhou and oversight of the Piantou passes, while Liu Ning was reassigned as left deputy commander-in-chief to help hold Datong.

sentences.zh: 二人並著功北邊，稱名將。

translations.literal: Both men won distinction on the northern frontier and were called famous generals.
translations.idiomatic: Both won fame on the northern frontier and were counted among the dynasty's best commanders.

sentences.zh: 璽以偏頭去太原遠，請改分守為鎮守，又以鎮守不當聽節制，乞易總兵銜。

translations.literal: Xi, because Piantou was far from Taiyuan, requested that divided command be changed to garrison command, and further that a garrison commander ought not to accept outside control, and begged to exchange for the commander-in-chief title.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xi argued that Piantou was too far from Taiyuan to be held under divided command, asked to be made garrison commander instead, and then petitioned to shed subordination to other officers by taking the full commander-in-chief title.

sentences.zh: 憲宗皆曲從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong in every case indulgently assented.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong granted every request.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，移鎮陜西，討平扶風諸縣附籍回回。

translations.literal: Early in Hongzhi he was transferred to garrison Shaanxi and suppressed the registered Hui communities of Fufeng and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi he was posted to Shaanxi and put down the registered Muslim communities in Fufeng and neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 三年佩征西將軍印，鎮守寧夏，甫一歲卒。

translations.literal: In the third year he wore the seal of General Who Conquers the West and garrisoned Ningxia; he had been there only one year when he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he took the seal of General Who Conquers the West and garrisoned Ningxia, but died after only a year in post.

sentences.zh: 且死，召諸子曰：「吾佩印分閫，分已足，獨未嘗大破敵，抱恨入地矣。

translations.literal: As he was about to die he summoned his sons and said: "I have worn the seal and held a separate command—the share was enough, yet I never once broke the enemy on a great scale; I carry regret into the earth.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he called his sons and said: "I wore the general's seal and held my own command—that was honor enough. Yet I never won a great victory over the enemy, and I go to my grave with that regret.

sentences.zh: 」連呼「殺賊」而瞑。

translations.literal: " He repeatedly cried "Kill the bandits!" and closed his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: " Again and again he cried, "Kill the enemy!"—and died.

sentences.zh: 子鵬，累官錦衣衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: His son Peng rose through offices to assistant commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Peng rose to assistant commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 璽歿後三年，而寧佩平羌將軍印，鎮甘肅。

translations.literal: Three years after Xi's death, Ning wore the seal of General Who Pacifies the Qiang and garrisoned Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Three years after Zhou Xi's death, Liu Ning took the seal of General Who Pacifies the Qiang and was posted to Gansu.

sentences.zh: 其冬，寇犯涼州，寧與戰抹山墩，擒斬五十余，相持至暮，收輜重南行。

translations.literal: That winter raiders violated Liangzhou; Ning fought them at Moshandun, captured and beheaded more than fifty, held the engagement until evening, gathered baggage train, and marched south.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when raiders struck Liangzhou, Liu Ning fought them at Moshandun, killed or captured more than fifty, battled until dusk, then gathered the baggage train and withdrew south.

sentences.zh: 寇復來襲，擒其長一人。

translations.literal: The raiders came again to attack, and he captured one of their chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders attacked again, and he took one of their leaders prisoner.

sentences.zh: 明日，參將顏玉來援，副將陶禎兵亦至，寇乃遁。

translations.literal: The next day assistant commander Yan Yu came to reinforce, deputy commander Tao Zhen's troops also arrived, and the raiders then fled.
translations.idiomatic: The next day assistant commander Yan Yu arrived with reinforcements, deputy commander Tao Zhen's force joined him, and the raiders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 俘其稚弱，獲馬駝牛羊二千，進右都督。

translations.literal: He took their women and children captive, seized two thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep, and was advanced to right commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He took women and children captive and seized two thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep, and was promoted to right commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 明年，與巡撫許進襲破土魯番於哈密，進左都督，增俸百石，以疾還京。

translations.literal: The next year, together with grand coordinator Xu Jin, he raided and broke Turfan at Hami; he was advanced to left commissioner-in-chief, given an increase of one hundred shi in salary, and returned to the capital on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he joined grand coordinator Xu Jin in a raid that broke Turfan at Hami; he was promoted to left commissioner-in-chief, granted an extra hundred shi of salary, and returned to the capital ill.

sentences.zh: 十三年，大同告警，命寧為副總兵，從平江伯陳銳禦之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Datong raised alarm; Ning was ordered to serve as deputy commander-in-chief and follow the Earl of Pingjiang, Chen Rui, to repel them.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, when Datong came under alarm, Liu Ning was made deputy commander-in-chief and sent with the Earl of Pingjiang, Chen Rui, to meet the threat.

sentences.zh: 銳無將略，與寧不協，止毋戰，寇遂得誌去，坐停半俸閑住。

translations.literal: Rui lacked generalship, was not in accord with Ning, and ordered no fighting; the raiders thus got their wish and left, and Ning was punished by suspension of half salary and idle residence.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Rui had no talent for command and clashed with Liu Ning; he forbade battle, the raiders withdrew as they pleased, and Liu Ning was punished with half pay and idle residence.

sentences.zh: 尋以參將贊畫朱暉軍務，亦無功。

translations.literal: Before long he served as assistant commander planning military affairs under Zhu Hui, and again achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was assigned as assistant commander to Zhu Hui's staff, but again won no success.

sentences.zh: 寧自陳哈密功，乞封伯，詔還全俸。

translations.literal: Ning himself stated his Hami merit and begged ennoblement as a marquis; an edict restored his full salary.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ning cited his Hami campaign in a petition for a marquisate; the court restored his full salary but did not grant the title.

sentences.zh: 寧有膽智，為大同副將時，入貢者數萬人懷異志。

translations.literal: Ning had courage and wit; when he was deputy commander at Datong, several tens of thousands among the tribute mission harbored rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ning was bold and shrewd. While deputy commander at Datong, he learned that tens of thousands among a tribute mission were nursing rebellious designs.

sentences.zh: 寧率二十騎直抵其營，眾駭愕。

translations.literal: Ning led twenty horsemen straight to their camp; the multitude was struck with alarm and astonishment.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ning rode in with only twenty men straight to their camp, stunning the whole assembly.

sentences.zh: 有部長勒馬引弓出。

translations.literal: One tribal chief reined his horse, drew his bow, and came out.
translations.idiomatic: One tribal chief spurred forward, bow drawn.

sentences.zh: 寧前下馬，與諸部長坐，舉策指畫，宣天子威德。

translations.literal: Ning went forward, dismounted, and sat with the various chiefs; raising his whip he gestured and explained, proclaiming the Son of Heaven's majesty and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ning dismounted, sat down with the chiefs, and with sweeping gestures spoke of the emperor's power and benevolence.

sentences.zh: 一人語不遜，寧摑其面，奮臂起，其長叱之退。

translations.literal: One man spoke insolently; Ning slapped his face, flung up his arm and rose, and the chief rebuked him and made him withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When one man spoke insolently, Liu Ning struck him across the face; the man started up angrily, but his chief shouted him down and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 寧復坐與語，呼酒歡飲，皆感悟，卒如約。

translations.literal: Ning sat again and spoke with them, called for wine and drank merrily; all were moved to understanding, and in the end they kept to the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ning sat down again, called for wine, and drank with them until all were reconciled; in the end they kept their pledge.

sentences.zh: 嘗仿古番上法，以五十八人為隊，隊伍重為陣，建五色幟。

translations.literal: He once modeled the ancient barbarian upward method: fifty-eight men formed a squad, squads layered into formations, and five-colored banners were raised.
translations.idiomatic: He once adapted an old nomadic battle formation, grouping fifty-eight men in a squad, stacking squads into larger units, and marking each with banners of five colors.

sentences.zh: 又各建五巨幟於中軍，中幟起，五陣各視其色應之，循環無端，每戰用是取勝。

translations.literal: He also raised five great banners in the central army; when the central banner rose, the five formations each looked to its color and responded, cycling without end—each battle he used this to win.
translations.idiomatic: He planted five great banners at headquarters; when the center banner rose, each of the five formations answered according to its color in an endless cycle—and with this signal system he won battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 晚再赴大同，已老病，帥又怯懦，故無成功，然孝宗朝良將稱寧。

translations.literal: Late in life he went again to Datong; he was already old and ill, and the commander was also timid, so there was no success—yet among good generals of the Xiaozong reign Ning was named.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he returned to Datong, but he was old and ill and his commander was timid, so nothing came of it; still, among Hongzhi-era commanders Liu Ning was counted among the best.

sentences.zh: 十七年卒，贈廣昌伯。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died; he was posthumously ennobled as Marquis of Guangchang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventeenth year of the reign and was posthumously ennobled as Marquis of Guangchang.

sentences.zh: 彭清，字源潔，榆林人。

translations.literal: Peng Qing, styled Yuanjie, was a man of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Qing, courtesy name Yuanjie, was from Yulin.

sentences.zh: 初襲綏德衛指揮使，以功擢都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: At first he inherited the post of regional commander of Suide Guard; for merit he was promoted to assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He first inherited command of Suide Guard and was promoted to assistant regional commander for his service.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，充右參將，分守肅州。

translations.literal: Early in Hongzhi he served as right assistant commander with divided command over Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi he became right assistant commander with divided command over Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 寇入犯，率兵躡之，獲馬駝器仗及所掠人畜而還。

translations.literal: When raiders entered to violate the border, he led troops in pursuit, seized horses, camels, weapons, and the people and livestock they had plundered, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders crossed the border he pursued them, recovered horses, camels, arms, and the people and livestock they had taken, and returned in triumph.

sentences.zh: 尋與巡撫王繼恢復哈密有功。

translations.literal: Before long, together with grand coordinator Wang Ji, he recovered Hami with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he distinguished himself alongside grand coordinator Wang Ji in the recovery of Hami.

sentences.zh: 清雖位偏校，而好謀有勇略，名聞中朝，尤為尚書馬文升所器。

translations.literal: Although Qing's rank was that of a minor officer, he loved planning and had courage and strategy; his name was heard at court, and he was especially valued by Minister Ma Wensheng.
translations.idiomatic: Though still a field officer of modest rank, Peng Qing was thoughtful and bold; his reputation reached the capital, and Minister Ma Wensheng held him in particular esteem.

sentences.zh: 嘗引疾乞休，文升力言於朝，慰留之。

translations.literal: Once he cited illness and begged to retire; Wensheng spoke forcefully at court and comforted and retained him.
translations.idiomatic: When he once asked to retire on grounds of illness, Ma Wensheng argued forcefully at court to keep him in service.

sentences.zh: 八年，甘肅有警，以文升薦，擢左副總兵，仍守甘肅。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Gansu raised alarm; on Wensheng's recommendation he was promoted to left deputy commander-in-chief and still guarded Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when Gansu came under threat, Ma Wensheng recommended him; he was promoted to left deputy commander-in-chief and remained on the Gansu frontier.

sentences.zh: 未幾，巡撫許進乞移清涼州。

translations.literal: Before long grand coordinator Xu Jin requested that Qing be moved to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long grand coordinator Xu Jin asked that Peng Qing be transferred to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 而是時哈密復為土魯番所據，文升方密圖恢復，倚清成功，言「肅州多故，而清名著西域，不可易」，乃寢。

translations.literal: But at that time Hami had again been seized by Turfan; Wensheng was secretly planning recovery and relied on Qing for success, saying "Suzhou has many troubles, and Qing's name is established in the Western Regions—it cannot be changed," and the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: But Hami had fallen to Turfan again, and Ma Wensheng was secretly planning its recovery and counting on Peng Qing; he argued that Suzhou was troubled enough and that Qing's name carried weight across the Western Regions, so the transfer was dropped.

sentences.zh: 文升既得楊翥策，銳欲搗哈密襲牙蘭，乃發罕東、赤斤暨哈密兵，令清統之為前鋒，從許進潛往。

translations.literal: Once Wensheng had obtained Yang Chong's plan, he keenly wished to strike Hami and raid Yalan; he then mobilized troops of Handom, Chijin, and Hami, ordered Qing to command them as vanguard, and secretly went with Xu Jin.
translations.idiomatic: After Ma Wensheng adopted Yang Chong's plan for a strike on Hami and a raid on Yalan, he mustered troops from Handom, Chijin, and Hami, put Peng Qing at their head as vanguard, and marched secretly with Xu Jin.

sentences.zh: 行半月，抵其城下，攻克之。

translations.literal: After half a month on the march they reached beneath its walls and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: After a fortnight's march they reached the city and took it.

sentences.zh: 牙蘭已先遁，乃撫安哈密遺種，全師而還。

translations.literal: Yalan had already fled beforehand; they then pacified and settled the remnant people of Hami and returned with the army intact.
translations.idiomatic: Yalan had already fled; they pacified Hami's remaining population and withdrew with the army intact.

sentences.zh: 是役也，文升授方略，擬從間道往，而進仍由故道，牙蘭遂逸去，斬獲無幾。

translations.literal: In this campaign Wensheng supplied the strategy and intended to go by a hidden route, but Jin still went by the old road; Yalan thus escaped, and beheadings and captures were few.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Wensheng had planned a flanking approach, but Xu Jin marched by the old road instead; Yalan escaped, and the haul of kills and captures was modest.

sentences.zh: 然番人素輕中國，謂不能涉其地，至是始知畏。

translations.literal: Yet the barbarians had long looked down on China, saying it could not cross their lands; only then did they first know fear.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier peoples had long scorned China as unable to reach their territory; this campaign taught them otherwise.

sentences.zh: 清功居多，稍遷都指揮使。

translations.literal: Qing's merit was the greater part; he was slightly promoted to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Qing's share of the credit was largest, and he was promoted to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 十年，總兵官劉寧罷，擢清都督僉事代之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year commander-in-chief Liu Ning was dismissed; Qing was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Liu Ning was removed as commander-in-chief, and Peng Qing was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief in his place.

sentences.zh: 其冬，土魯番歸哈密忠順王陜巴，且乞通貢，西域復定。

translations.literal: That winter Turfan restored Hami's loyal and obedient prince Shaan Ba and also begged to resume tribute; the Western Regions were again settled.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Turfan restored Hami's loyal prince Shaan Ba and petitioned to resume tribute, and the Western Regions were pacified once more.

sentences.zh: 屢辭疾，請解兵柄，不允。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he declined on grounds of illness and requested to relinquish military authority; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to retire on grounds of illness and surrender his command, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 十五年卒。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifteenth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 清禦士有恩，久鎮西陲，威名甚著，番夷憚之。

translations.literal: Qing treated his soldiers with kindness; he long garrisoned the western frontier, his formidable name was very prominent, and the barbarians feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Qing treated his men with kindness; after long service on the western frontier his reputation was formidable, and the frontier peoples feared him.

sentences.zh: 性廉潔，在鎮遭母及妻妹四喪，貧不能歸葬。

translations.literal: By nature he was incorrupt and clean; while at his garrison he suffered four bereavements—mother and wife's sisters—and was too poor to return and bury them.
translations.idiomatic: He was incorruptible; while on post he lost his mother and three sisters-in-law in succession and was too poor to send their bodies home for burial.

sentences.zh: 卒之日，將士及庶民婦豎皆流涕。

translations.literal: On the day of his death, officers, soldiers, and common people, women and children alike, all wept.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died, soldiers and civilians alike—men, women, and children—all wept.

sentences.zh: 遺命其子不得受賻贈，故其喪亦不能歸。

translations.literal: He left instructions that his son must not accept funeral gifts, and therefore his funeral also could not be returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He left orders that his son accept no funeral gifts, and so even his own body could not be sent home.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，命撫臣發帑錢，資送歸裏，賜祭葬如制。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and ordered the grand coordinator to disburse treasury money to provide funds for sending him home, and granted sacrificial and burial honors according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this, he ordered the provincial governor to pay from the treasury for the journey home and granted the prescribed funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 姜漢，榆林衛人。

translations.literal: Jiang Han was a man of Yulin Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Han was from Yulin Guard.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，嗣世職，為本衛指揮使。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi reign he succeeded to the hereditary office and became regional commander of his own guard.
translations.idiomatic: During Hongzhi he inherited the family post and became commander of Yulin Guard.

sentences.zh: 御史胡希顏薦其材勇，進都指揮僉事，充延綏遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: Censor Hu Xiyan recommended his talent and bravery; he was promoted to assistant regional commander and appointed mobile corps general of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Hu Xiyan praised his ability and courage, and he was promoted to assistant regional commander and made mobile corps general of Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 十八年春，寇犯寧夏興武營。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighteenth year raiders violated Ningxia's Xingwu Camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighteenth year raiders struck Xingwu Camp in Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 漢帥所部馳援，遇於中沙墩，擊敗之。

translations.literal: Han led his command in rapid relief, met them at Zhongshadun, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Han led his troops in haste to the rescue, met the enemy at Zhongshadun, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 賜敕獎勞。

translations.literal: An imperial edict of commendation and reward was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an edict commending and rewarding him.

sentences.zh: 武宗嗣位，寇大舉犯宣、大，漢偕副總兵曹雄、參將王戟分道援，有功。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong succeeded to the throne, raiders invaded on a large scale against Xuanfu and Datong; Han together with deputy commander-in-chief Cao Xiong and assistant commander Wang Ji went to the rescue by separate routes and achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wuzong emperor took the throne, raiders struck Xuanfu and Datong in force; Jiang Han, deputy commander Cao Xiong, and assistant commander Wang Ji relieved them by separate routes and won credit.

sentences.zh: 尋代雄為副總兵，協守延綏。

translations.literal: Before long he replaced Xiong as deputy commander-in-chief and jointly guarded Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: He soon replaced Cao Xiong as deputy commander and shared command over Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 正德三年移守涼州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengde he was transferred to guard Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 3 he was transferred to the Liangzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，擢署都督僉事，充總兵官，鎮寧夏。

translations.literal: The next year in winter he was promoted to acting assistant commissioner-in-chief, made supreme commander, and garrisoned Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter he was promoted to acting assistant commissioner-in-chief, made commander-in-chief, and posted to Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 漢馭軍嚴整，得將士心。

translations.literal: Han governed the army with strict order and won the hearts of officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Han ran a tight army and won the loyalty of his officers and men.

sentences.zh: 甫數月而安化王寘鐇謀逆，置酒召漢及巡撫安惟學等宴。

translations.literal: After only a few months the Prince of Anhua, Zhi Fan, plotted rebellion; he set out wine and summoned Han and grand coordinator An Weixue and others to a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Only a few months later the Prince of Anhua, Zhi Fan, plotted treason and invited Jiang Han, grand coordinator An Weixue, and others to a feast.

sentences.zh: 酒半，其黨何錦等率眾入，即座上執漢。

translations.literal: When the wine was half finished, his faction led by He Jin and others entered with a crowd and seized Han right at his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-feast, his followers He Jin and the rest burst in and seized Jiang Han at the table.

sentences.zh: 漢奮起，怒罵不屈，遂殺之。

translations.literal: Han rose up in anger, cursed them without yielding, and they thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Han sprang up, cursed them to the last, and they killed him.

sentences.zh: 子奭逃免。

translations.literal: His son Shi escaped and survived.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 賊平，訟於朝。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, the case was brought before the court.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed, the matter was brought before the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔賜祭葬。

translations.literal: An edict granted sacrificial honors and burial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered state funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 有司為立祠，春秋祭之。

translations.literal: The local officials erected a shrine for him and sacrificed to him in spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: The local authorities built him a shrine and held rites each spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖時，復從巡撫張珩請，賜額「憫忠」。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign, again following grand coordinator Zhang Heng's request, the title plaque "Commiserating Loyalty" was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiajing, on grand coordinator Zhang Heng's petition, the shrine was granted the inscription "Lamenting Loyalty."

sentences.zh: 奭當嗣職，帝以漢死事，特進一官，為都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Shi was due to succeed to the office; because Han died in the performance of duty, the emperor specially advanced him one rank to assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was heir to the post; because Jiang Han had died in service, the emperor promoted him one rank to assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 十一年，回賊魏景陽作亂，華陰諸縣悉被害，巡撫蕭翀檄奭討之，獲景陽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, the Hui rebel Wei Jingyang raised rebellion; all the counties of Huayin suffered harm; grand coordinator Xiao Chong ordered Shi by dispatch to suppress him, and he captured Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Hui rebel Wei Jingyang revolted and ravaged the counties of Huayin; grand coordinator Xiao Chong ordered Shi to campaign against him, and he captured Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 進署都指揮同知，充右參將守肅州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to acting vice regional commander and appointed right assistant commander guarding Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting vice regional commander and made right assistant commander of the Suzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年，擢右副總兵，分守涼州，進署都督僉事，充總兵官，鎮甘肅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing he was promoted to right deputy commander-in-chief with divided command over Liangzhou, advanced to acting assistant commissioner-in-chief, made supreme commander, and garrisoned Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 2 he became right deputy commander with divided command over Liangzhou, was raised to acting assistant commissioner-in-chief, made commander-in-chief, and posted to Gansu.

sentences.zh: 回賊犯甘州，奭與戰張欽堡，敗走之。

translations.literal: Hui rebels violated Ganzhou; Shi fought them at Zhangqin Fort and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui rebels attacked Ganzhou, Shi fought them at Zhangqin Fort and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 未幾，西海賊八千騎犯涼州。

translations.literal: Before long, eight thousand horsemen of the Western Sea raiders violated Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long eight thousand Western Sea raiders struck Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 奭率遊擊周倫等襲擊於苦水墩，大敗之，斬首百余級，殲其長，還所掠人口千二百、畜產二千。

translations.literal: Shi led mobile corps commander Zhou Lun and others in a surprise attack at Kushuidun, inflicting a great defeat, beheading more than one hundred heads, destroying their chief, and recovering one thousand two hundred captured persons and two thousand head of livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Shi led mobile corps commander Zhou Lun and others in a raid at Kushuidun, won a crushing victory, took more than a hundred heads, killed their leader, and recovered twelve hundred captives and two thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 都指揮張錦亦戰死。

translations.literal: Regional commander Zhang Jin also died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Zhang Jin also fell in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 錄功，進署都督同知。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was advanced to acting vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: His victory was entered on the rolls and he was promoted to acting vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 吉囊他部寇莊浪，奭與遇分水嶺，再勝之。

translations.literal: Another band of Jinang raided Zhuanglang; Shi met them at Fen Shuiling and again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Another Jinang band raided Zhuanglang; Shi met them at Fen Shuiling and defeated them again.

sentences.zh: 遂至平嶺。

translations.literal: He then pursued to Pingling.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued them as far as Pingling.

sentences.zh: 敵騎大集，奭伏兵誘之，復斬其長一人，獲首功七十，予實授。

translations.literal: The enemy horsemen massed in force; Shi used ambush troops to lure them, again beheaded one of their chiefs, obtained seventy heads as merit, and was granted the appointment in full.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy cavalry massed, Shi laid an ambush, killed another chieftain, took seventy heads, and received a permanent commission.

sentences.zh: 十六年春，寇大入甘州，不能禦，貶二秩戴罪。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixteenth year raiders entered Ganzhou on a large scale; he could not repel them and was reduced two ranks to serve at fault.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixteenth year raiders poured into Ganzhou; failing to stop them, he was demoted two ranks and ordered to redeem his fault.

sentences.zh: 尋以永昌破敵功，復署都督僉事。

translations.literal: Before long, for merit in defeating the enemy at Yongchang, he was again given acting assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, for a victory at Yongchang, he was restored to acting assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 其冬，坐前罪罷。

translations.literal: That winter he was dismissed for his previous offense.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was dismissed on account of his earlier fault.

sentences.zh: 久之，以薦擢副總兵，協守大同，為總督翁萬達劾罷，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time, on recommendation he was promoted to deputy commander-in-chief and jointly guarded Datong; he was impeached and dismissed by supreme commander Weng Wanda and died.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was recommended for deputy commander and shared command over Datong, but supreme commander Weng Wanda impeached and dismissed him; he died.

sentences.zh: 子應熊，嗣指揮使，擢宣府西路參將。

translations.literal: His son Yingxiong inherited the post as regional commander and was promoted to assistant commander of the western route of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yingxiong inherited command and was promoted to assistant commander on Xuanfu's western route.

sentences.zh: 二十七年春，俺答寇大同，總兵官周尚文戰曹家莊，應熊從萬達自懷來鼓噪揚塵而西。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-seventh year, Altan raided Datong; supreme commander Zhou Shangwen fought at Caojiazhuang, and Yingxiong following Wanda from Huailai made a clamor and raised dust westward.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-seventh year Altan raided Datong while commander Zhou Shangwen fought at Caojiazhuang; Yingxiong followed Wanda from Huailai, raising dust and clamor to the west.

sentences.zh: 寇不測眾寡，遂遁。

translations.literal: The raiders could not gauge whether their numbers were many or few, and thereupon fled.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to tell friend from foe, the raiders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 累進都督僉事，充總兵官，鎮守寧夏。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached assistant commissioner-in-chief, served as supreme commander, and garrisoned Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to assistant commissioner-in-chief, became commander-in-chief, and was posted to Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，套寇數萬騎屯賀蘭山，遣精騎掠紅井。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, tens of thousands of Ordos raiders encamped at Helan Mountain and sent elite horsemen to plunder Hongjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year tens of thousands of Ordos horsemen camped on Helan Mountain and sent picked riders to raid Hongjing.

sentences.zh: 應熊戒將士固守以綴敵，而潛師攻敵營，斬首百四十級，進都督同知。

translations.literal: Yingxiong ordered officers and soldiers to hold firm to pin down the enemy, while a hidden force attacked the enemy camp, beheading one hundred forty heads, and he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiong held his men in a tight defense to pin the enemy while a hidden column struck their camp, took one hundred forty heads, and earned promotion to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 越二年，套寇數萬踏冰西渡，由寧夏山後直抵莊涼。

translations.literal: Two years later, tens of thousands of Ordos raiders crossed westward on the ice and, via the rear of the Ningxia mountains, went straight to Zhuangliang.
translations.idiomatic: Two years on, tens of thousands of Ordos raiders crossed the ice westward and, coming behind the Ningxia range, drove straight into Zhuangliang.

sentences.zh: 應熊等掩擊，獲首功百余，進右都督。

translations.literal: Yingxiong and others launched a surprise attack, obtained more than one hundred heads as merit, and he was promoted to right commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiong and his men caught them in a surprise attack, took more than a hundred heads, and he was promoted to right commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 御史崔揀劾其縱寇，褫職逮問，充為事官，赴塞上立功。

translations.literal: Censor Cui Jian impeached him for letting raiders go; his office was stripped and he was arrested for investigation, made an officer on probation, and sent to the frontier to achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Cui Jian accused him of letting raiders escape; he was stripped of rank, seized for trial, reduced to probationary office, and sent to the frontier to redeem himself by service.

sentences.zh: 四十年秋，寇六萬余騎犯居庸岔道口，應熊被圍於南溝，中五槍墮馬，參將胡鎮殺數人奪之歸。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fortieth year, more than sixty thousand horsemen raiders violated Juyong Cha Pass; Yingxiong was surrounded at Nangou, struck by five spears and fell from his horse; assistant commander Hu Zhen killed several men and rescued him.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fortieth year more than sixty thousand raiders struck Juyong Pass; Yingxiong was surrounded at Nangou, took five spears and fell from his horse; assistant commander Hu Zhen cut down several enemies and brought him back alive.

sentences.zh: 其冬，復為右都督，充總兵官，鎮守大同。

translations.literal: That winter he was again made right commissioner-in-chief, served as supreme commander, and garrisoned Datong.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was restored as right commissioner-in-chief, made commander-in-chief, and posted to Datong.

sentences.zh: 以招徠塞外人口，增俸一級。

translations.literal: For drawing in population from beyond the passes, his salary was increased one grade.
translations.idiomatic: He was given one step in pay for bringing outsiders in from beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，寇大舉犯畿輔，詔應熊等入援，諸鎮兵盡集，見敵勢盛，不敢擊。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, raiders invaded on a large scale against the capital region; an edict ordered Yingxiong and others to enter as relief; troops from all garrisons assembled, but seeing the enemy strength they dared not strike.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year raiders struck the capital region in force; Yingxiong and others were ordered to the relief, but though troops from every garrison gathered, none dared attack given the enemy's strength.

sentences.zh: 給事中李瑜遂劾應熊及宣大總督江東、保定總兵官祝福坐視胡鎮被圍，一卒不發。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Li Yu thereupon impeached Yingxiong, Xuan-Datong supreme commander Jiang Dong, and Baoding supreme commander Zhu Fu for sitting and watching while Hu Zhen was surrounded, not dispatching a single soldier.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Li Yu impeached Yingxiong along with Xuan-Datong governor Jiang Dong and Baoding commander Zhu Fu for doing nothing while Hu Zhen was surrounded—not a single man sent.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，降敕嚴責。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and issued a sternly reproving edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and sent a sharply worded rebuke.

sentences.zh: 會寇將遁，應熊禦之密雲，頗有斬獲。

translations.literal: Just as the raiders were about to flee, Yingxiong met them at Miyun and had considerable beheadings and captures.
translations.idiomatic: As the raiders were preparing to withdraw, Yingxiong engaged them at Miyun and took a fair number of heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 寇退，帝令江東第諸將功，以應熊為首，詔增其祖職二級。

translations.literal: When the raiders withdrew, the emperor ordered Jiang Dong to rank the generals' merit with Yingxiong first, and an edict increased his ancestral office two grades.
translations.idiomatic: After the raiders withdrew, the emperor had Jiang Dong rank the generals' merits with Yingxiong at the top and ordered his hereditary rank raised by two steps.

sentences.zh: 已，錄防秋勞，進左都督。

translations.literal: Before long, recording his autumn-defense labors, he was advanced to left commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon rewarded for frontier defense that autumn with promotion to left commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 總督趙炳然劾其縱寇互市，殘害朔州，坐戍邊。

translations.literal: Supreme commander Zhao Bingran impeached him for letting raiders go and for the border-market trade that harmed Shuozhou; he was sentenced to frontier banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme commander Zhao Bingran accused him of tolerating raiders and border trade that ravaged Shuozhou, and he was sentenced to military exile on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，赦還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, he was pardoned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Longqing emperor ascended the throne, he was pardoned and allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 子顯祚襲職，累官署都督僉事，總兵官，歷鎮山西、宣府。

translations.literal: His son Xianzuo inherited the office, rose through successive posts to acting assistant commissioner-in-chief and supreme commander, and successively garrisoned Shanxi and Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xianzuo inherited the post, rose to acting assistant commissioner-in-chief and commander-in-chief, and served at Shanxi and Xuanfu in turn.

sentences.zh: 子弼，亦至都督僉事，為援遼總兵官。

translations.literal: His son Bi also reached assistant commissioner-in-chief and served as supreme commander for the Liaodong relief force.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bi likewise became assistant commissioner-in-chief and served as commander of the Liaodong relief army.
