sentences.zh: 姜氏為大將，著邊功，凡五世。

translations.literal: The Jiang clan produced great generals and achieved frontier merit through five generations.
translations.idiomatic: For five generations the Jiang family produced senior commanders renowned for service on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 安國，字良臣，綏德衛人。

translations.literal: An Guo, styled Liangchen, was a man of Suide Guard.
translations.idiomatic: An Guo, courtesy name Liangchen, was from Suide Guard.

sentences.zh: 初為諸生，通《春秋》子史，知名里中。

translations.literal: At first he was a licentiate, mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals and the masters and histories, and was known in the locality.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a scholar, mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals and the classical histories, and was known in his home district.

sentences.zh: 後襲世職，為指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Later he inherited the hereditary office and became assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He later inherited the family post and became assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 正德三年中武會舉第一，進署指揮使，赴陜西三邊立功。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengde he ranked first in the military metropolitan examination, was promoted to acting regional commander, and went to the three border districts of Shaanxi to achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 3 he topped the military metropolitan exam, was made acting regional commander, and went to serve on merit on the Shaanxi frontier.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾要賄，國同舉六十人鹹無貲，瑾乃編之行伍，有警聽調，禁其擅歸。

translations.literal: Liu Jin demanded bribes; Guo and the sixty who had passed the examination alike had no money; Jin then enrolled them in the ranks, to be mobilized when alarms arose and forbidden to return on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin demanded bribes; Guo and all sixty successful candidates had none to give, so Jin posted them as ordinary soldiers—called up when alarms sounded and barred from leaving without orders.

sentences.zh: 六十人者悉大窘，儕於戍卒，不聊生。

translations.literal: All sixty were greatly distressed, treated on a par with frontier garrison soldiers, and could not make a living.
translations.idiomatic: All sixty were reduced to dire straits, treated no better than garrison conscripts, and could barely survive.

sentences.zh: 而邊臣憚瑾，竟無有收恤之者。

translations.literal: Yet frontier officials feared Jin, and in the end none took them in or showed them kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials feared Jin, and in the end none would take them in or help them.

sentences.zh: 寘鐇反，肆赦，始放還。

translations.literal: When Zhi Fan rebelled, a general amnesty was proclaimed and they were at last released to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi Fan rebelled, a general amnesty was proclaimed and they were finally allowed to go home.

sentences.zh: 通政叢蘭請收用，瑾怒，諷給事中張瓚等劾諸人皆庸才，悉停其加官。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner of the Messenger Bureau Cong Lan requested they be recruited for service; Jin was angry and had supervising secretaries Zhang Zan and others impeach that all these men were mediocre talents, and all their promotions were halted.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Cong Lan asked that they be employed, but Jin was angry and prompted supervising secretaries including Zhang Zan to impeach them all as mediocrities, and every promotion was blocked.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，始以故官分守寧夏西路。

translations.literal: After Jin was executed, he was at last restored to his former office with divided command over the western route of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's execution he was restored to his former rank and given divided command over western Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 尋進署都指揮僉事，充右參將，擢右副總兵，協守大同，徙延綏。

translations.literal: Before long he was advanced to acting assistant regional commander, appointed right assistant commander, promoted to right deputy commander-in-chief, jointly guarded Datong, and was transferred to Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon raised to acting assistant regional commander, made right assistant commander, promoted to right deputy commander, shared command over Datong, and was transferred to Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 十一年冬，寇二萬騎分掠偏頭關諸處，國偕遊擊杭雄馳敗之岢嵐州，斬首八十余級，獲馬千余匹。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year twenty thousand horsemen raided separately at places such as Piantou Pass; Guo together with mobile corps commander Hang Xiong raced to defeat them at Kelan Prefecture, beheading more than eighty heads and seizing more than one thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: That winter twenty thousand horsemen raided in bands around Piantou Pass; Guo and mobile corps commander Hang Xiong raced to Kelan Prefecture, routed them, took more than eighty heads, and captured over a thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 寇遂遁。

translations.literal: The raiders thereupon fled.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders fled.

sentences.zh: 初，寇大入白羊口，帝遣中官張忠、都督劉暉、侍郎丁鳳統京軍討之，比至，已飽掠去。

translations.literal: Earlier, when raiders had entered on a large scale at Baiyang Pass, the emperor dispatched eunuch Zhang Zhong, commissioner-in-chief Liu Hui, and vice minister Ding Feng to lead the capital army against them; by the time they arrived, the raiders had already plundered their fill and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when raiders poured through Baiyang Pass, the emperor sent eunuch Zhang Zhong, commissioner Liu Hui, and Vice Minister Ding Feng at the head of capital troops—but by the time they arrived the raiders had already sacked what they wanted and withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 忠、暉恥無功，紀功御史劉澄甫攘國等功歸之，大行遷賞，忠等悉增祿，予世蔭。

translations.literal: Zhong and Hui were ashamed of having no merit; merit-recording censor Liu Chengfu appropriated the merit of Guo and others to them; lavish promotions and rewards were bestowed; Zhong and the rest all had their salaries increased and were granted hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and Hui were shamed by their empty record; merit censor Liu Chengfu credited Guo's victory to them instead, triggering lavish rewards—salary increases and hereditary privileges for Zhong and his party.

sentences.zh: 尚書王瓊亦加少保，蔭子錦衣。

translations.literal: Minister Wang Qiong also received the added title of Junior Guardian, and his son was granted Embroidered Uniform Guard privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Qiong was made Junior Guardian as well, and his son received Embroidered Uniform Guard hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 國時以署都督僉事為寧夏總兵官，僅予實授，意不平，不敢自列，乃具疏力辭，為部卒重傷者乞敘錄。

translations.literal: Guo at the time served as acting assistant commissioner-in-chief and Ningxia supreme commander but was granted only a permanent commission at that level; he was resentful but did not dare list himself; he thereupon submitted a memorial earnestly declining, and begged merit recording for troops under his command who had been severely wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Guo was then acting assistant commissioner-in-chief and Ningxia commander-in-chief, yet received only a permanent appointment at that rank; indignant but unwilling to petition for himself, he submitted a memorial firmly declining credit and begged rewards for badly wounded men under his command.

sentences.zh: 瓊請再敘國功，始進都督同知。

translations.literal: Qiong requested that Guo's merit be recorded again, and he was at last advanced to vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiong asked that Guo's merit be entered again, and he was finally promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 當是時，佞幸擅朝，債帥風大熾，獨國以材武致大將。

translations.literal: At that time, favored sycophants dominated the court and the fashion of debt-ridden commanders was greatly rampant; Guo alone, through talent in military affairs, reached the rank of great general.
translations.idiomatic: At that time favored favorites ran the court and bought-off generals were everywhere; only Guo, through genuine talent and martial skill, rose to senior command.

sentences.zh: 端謹練戎務，所至思盡職，推將材者必歸焉。

translations.literal: Upright and careful, practiced in military affairs, wherever he went he thought to fulfill his duty; those recommending commanders' talent invariably pointed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and diligent, skilled in military affairs, he gave his full duty wherever he served; anyone asked to name a capable commander pointed to him.

sentences.zh: 在鎮四年卒。

translations.literal: After four years at his garrison he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died after four years in command.

sentences.zh: 特謚武敏。

translations.literal: He was specially granted the posthumous title Wumin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Wumin, "Martially Keen."

sentences.zh: 杭雄，字世威，世為綏德衛總旗。

translations.literal: Hang Xiong, styled Shiwei, for generations was centurion of Suide Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Hang Xiong, courtesy name Shiwei, came from a family of centurions at Suide Guard.

sentences.zh: 雄承蔭，數先登，積首功，六遷至指揮使。

translations.literal: Xiong inherited privilege, several times was first to ascend, accumulated head-merit, and through six promotions reached regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong inherited his father's privilege, repeatedly led the assault, piled up head counts, and rose through six promotions to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 正德七年進署都指揮僉事，剿賊四川，尋守備西寧。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhengde he was advanced to acting assistant regional commander, suppressed bandits in Sichuan, and soon after garrisoned Xining.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 7 he was promoted to acting assistant regional commander, campaigned against bandits in Sichuan, and was soon posted to Xining.

sentences.zh: 用尚書楊一清薦，擢延綏遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: On Minister Yang Yiqing's recommendation he was promoted to mobile corps general of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: On Minister Yang Yiqing's recommendation he was made mobile corps general of Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 從都御史彭澤經略哈密，偕副將安國破敵岢嵐，進都督僉事。

translations.literal: Following Censor-in-Chief Peng Ze in managing Hami affairs, together with Deputy Commander An Guo he defeated the enemy at Kelan and was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Censor-in-Chief Peng Ze in frontier affairs at Hami, and with Deputy Commander An Guo routed the enemy at Kelan, earning promotion to assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 改參將，擢都督同知，統邊兵操於西內。

translations.literal: He was changed to assistant commander, promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief, and commanded frontier troops in drill within the Western Inner Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as assistant commander, promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief, and drilled frontier troops in the Western Inner Enclosure.

sentences.zh: 武宗幸宣府、大同，雄扈從，即拜大同總兵官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong visited Xuanfu and Datong, Xiong escorted him and was immediately appointed supreme commander of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wuzong emperor toured Xuanfu and Datong, Xiong accompanied him and was immediately made commander of Datong.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，汰傳奉官，雄當貶，以方守邊，命署都督僉事，鎮守如故。

translations.literal: Early in Jiajing, honorary appointees were cut; Xiong was due for demotion, but because he was then guarding the frontier he was ordered to serve as acting assistant commissioner-in-chief with garrison command unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiajing, when honorary appointees were purged, Xiong should have been demoted, but because he was holding the frontier he was kept as acting assistant commissioner-in-chief with his command unchanged.

sentences.zh: 小王子萬余騎入沙河堡，雄戰卻之。

translations.literal: The Lesser Prince entered Shahe Fort with more than ten thousand horsemen; Xiong fought and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser Prince led more than ten thousand horsemen into Shahe Fort; Xiong fought them off.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復大入，不能禦，求罷不許。

translations.literal: Before long they again entered on a large scale; he could not repel them and requested dismissal but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they raided again in force; unable to stop them, he asked to resign but was refused.

sentences.zh: 移延綏，召僉書後軍都督府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Yan-sui and summoned to serve as registrar of the Rear Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Yan-sui and called to serve as registrar of the Rear Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，土魯番侵甘肅，詔尚書金獻民視師，以雄佩平虜大將軍印，充總兵官，提督陜西、延綏、寧夏、甘肅四鎮軍務。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year Turfan invaded Gansu; an edict ordered Minister Jin Xianmin to inspect the army; Xiong was invested with the seal of the Great General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, made supreme commander, and given overall supervision of military affairs in the four garrisons of Shaanxi, Yan-sui, Ningxia, and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the third year Turfan invaded Gansu; Minister Jin Xianmin was sent to oversee the campaign; Xiong was given the seal of Great General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, made commander-in-chief, and placed in charge of all four frontier garrisons—Shaanxi, Yan-sui, Ningxia, and Gansu.

sentences.zh: 列侯出征，始佩大將軍印，無授都督者，至是特以命雄。

translations.literal: When ranked marquises went on campaign they first received the great general's seal; none had been granted to a commissioner-in-chief; only at this time was it specially conferred on Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: When marquises took the field they alone had borne the great general's seal—never before given to a commissioner-in-chief; Xiong was the first to receive it.

sentences.zh: 甫至，寇已破走，而雄亦得蔭錦衣千戶。

translations.literal: As soon as he arrived the raiders had already been defeated and driven off, yet Xiong also received Embroidered Uniform Guard thousand-household hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: He arrived only after the enemy had already been routed, yet Xiong still received hereditary privilege as an Embroidered Uniform Guard thousand-household.

sentences.zh: 既班師，復出鎮寧夏。

translations.literal: After the army returned he again went out to garrison Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: After the troops withdrew he returned to command at Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 吉囊大入，總督王憲檄雄等破之，進都督同知。

translations.literal: Jinang entered on a large scale; supreme commander Wang Xian ordered Xiong and others to defeat him; he was advanced to vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinang invaded in force, supreme commander Wang Xian ordered Xiong to defeat him; he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 寇八千騎乘冰犯寧夏。

translations.literal: Eight thousand horsemen raiders crossed the ice to violate Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: Eight thousand raiders crossed the ice into Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 雄及副總兵趙鎮禦之，前鋒陷伏中，雄等皆敗。

translations.literal: Xiong and deputy commander-in-chief Zhao Zhen met them in defense; the vanguard fell into an ambush and Xiong and the rest were all defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong and deputy commander Zhao Zhen tried to stop them, but the vanguard walked into an ambush and they were routed.

sentences.zh: 總督王瓊劾之，奪官閑住。

translations.literal: Supreme commander Wang Qiong impeached them; their offices were stripped and they were placed in idle residence.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme commander Wang Qiong impeached them; Xiong was stripped of rank and sent into retirement.

sentences.zh: 明年卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 雄敢戰。

translations.literal: Xiong was bold in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was fearless in combat.

sentences.zh: 嘗以數騎行邊，敵麕至。

translations.literal: Once with only a few horsemen he patrolled the border when the enemy arrived in swarms.
translations.idiomatic: Once, riding the frontier with only a handful of men, he found the enemy closing in from every side.

sentences.zh: 乃下馬積鞍為壘，跪而射之。

translations.literal: He dismounted, piled saddles into a barricade, knelt, and shot at them.
translations.idiomatic: He dismounted, heaped saddles into a breastwork, knelt behind it, and shot.

sentences.zh: 敵退，解衣，腋凝血，乃知中飛矢。

translations.literal: When the enemy withdrew he removed his coat; clotted blood under his arm showed he had been struck by a flying arrow.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy drew off he stripped off his coat and found clotted blood under his arm—only then did he know a stray arrow had found him.

sentences.zh: 武宗在大同，見雄氈帷敝甚，曰：「老杭窮乃爾。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong was at Datong and saw Xiong's felt curtain very worn, saying: "Old Hang is poor indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong was at Datong and saw how threadbare Hang Xiong's felt tent was. "So old Hang is this poor," he said.

sentences.zh: 」寇至，帝將親擊。

translations.literal: " When raiders came the emperor was about to strike in person.
translations.idiomatic: " When raiders arrived, the emperor prepared to fight in person.

sentences.zh: 雄叩馬諫曰：「主人畜犬，不使吠盜，奚用犬為？

translations.literal: Xiong seized the bridle and remonstrated, saying: "If a master keeps a dog and will not let it bark at thieves, what use is the dog?
translations.idiomatic: Xiong caught the emperor's bridle and pleaded: "If a man keeps dogs but will not let them bark at thieves, what good are the dogs?

sentences.zh: 願聽臣等效力。

translations.literal: I beg that you allow your servants to exert our strength.
translations.idiomatic: Let your servants do the fighting instead."

sentences.zh: 」帝笑而止。

translations.literal: " The emperor laughed and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor laughed and gave up the idea.

sentences.zh: 少役延綏巡撫行臺，既貴，每至臺議事，不敢正席坐，曰：「此當年役所也。

translations.literal: In youth he had served at the Yan-sui grand coordinator's mobile office; once eminent, whenever he came to the office to discuss affairs he would not sit squarely on the seat, saying: "This was where I served in my younger days.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had been a runner at the Yan-sui grand coordinator's field office. After he rose high, whenever he came there for council he would not take the main seat, saying, "This is where I used to serve."

sentences.zh: 」正德、嘉靖間，西北名將，馬永而下稱雄雲。

translations.literal: " Among northwestern generals from the Zhengde and Jiajing reigns, after Ma Yong, Xiong was ranked foremost.
translations.idiomatic: " Among the great generals of the northwest in the Zhengde and Jiajing reigns, from Ma Yong downward, Xiong was held first in esteem.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：時平則將略無由見。

translations.literal: The praise says: In peaceful times a general's stratagem has no occasion to appear.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: In times of peace a commander's talent for war has no chance to show itself.

sentences.zh: 或綰符出鎮，守疆禦侮，著有勞效，以功名終，亦足尚矣。

translations.literal: Some bound the tally and went out to garrison frontiers, guarded the borders and repelled insult, achieved manifest merit, and ended in fame and office—these are also worthy of respect.
translations.idiomatic: Yet some took command beyond the passes, held the frontier and beat back invasion, left a clear record of service, and finished their lives in honor—such men are still worth our regard.

sentences.zh: 許貴、周賢、魯鑒、姜漢家世為將，勛閥相承，而賢與漢死事尤烈。

translations.literal: Xu Gui, Zhou Xian, Lu Jian, and Jiang Han came from generations of generals, ennobled houses succeeding one another; yet Xian and Han died in service most heroically.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gui, Zhou Xian, Lu Jian, and Jiang Han were soldiers' sons for generations, noble houses in unbroken line; yet Xian and Han died in the field most fiercely of all.

sentences.zh: 彭清、杭雄之清節，斯又其最優者歟。

translations.literal: The upright integrity of Peng Qing and Hang Xiong—are these not the finest among them?
translations.idiomatic: The stainless integrity of Peng Qing and Hang Xiong—were these not the finest of the company?
